# DEV.md — where the project is, and how to move it forward

The starting point for any development session on Choupo.  Read this + `CLAUDE.md`
(the always-loaded brief) and you know the state, the settled contracts, and the
next work — no need to reconstruct it from scattered notes.  Companion to
[`RELEASING.md`](RELEASING.md) (how to cut a release) — this file is *where we
are and what to do next*.

*Last synced 2026-08-04.  Verify any number against the tree before relying on it —
and prefer `generated/releaseInventory.json` to any number written in prose.*

---

> **Development style (Vítor, 2026-08-23):** real problem -> fix the cause ->
> smallest useful test -> stop.  No new gate, framework, manifest, tier or
> policy without a real observed failure that demands it; remove machinery
> whose purpose has ended; every piece of work explainable in plain language
> (what was wrong, what changed, how we know it is better).  The verification
> layer serves the simulator, never the reverse -- and no meta-mechanism to
> enforce this rule: it is applied by judgement, which is the point.

## 1. Current state (facts, not history)

- **Branches (revised 2026-07-29):** `main` **is** `Choupo-dev` — the default
  branch carries the continuously-updated development line, no pre-announced
  target version.  **Work happens on `main`.**  A release is an immutable tag
  `vYYMM`; a `release-YYMM` branch is cut from that tag only on the day a patch
  actually ships.  `dev` is retired.  Rationale and procedure: `RELEASING.md`.
- **Latest release:** `Choupo-2608` — immutable git tag `v2608`, patched as
  `v2608.1` (packaging only: the frozen app's engine paths; the engine, the
  citation and the public name are unchanged).  Its frozen browser copy at
  `choupo.org/v2608/app/` IS published, built from `v2608.1` by
  `freeze-app.yml`, and was driven in a browser: every engine request stays
  inside its prefix and the answer reproduces the release's own golden.
  (`Choupo-2607` was withdrawn on 2026-09-02.)  `main` is tagged as the next
  `Choupo-YYMM` when the project has something worth freezing (decided at cut
  time, never pre-committed — 2607 to 2608 was seven weeks, so no cadence is
  promised anywhere).  This paragraph said the frozen copy was NOT published
  for most of 2026-09-02, and went on saying so after it was — corrected the
  same night.
- **Site:** served by a SECOND repository, `choupo-admin/choupo-admin.github.io`
  — it holds the `CNAME` and any frozen `/vYYMM/app/`.  This repo only BUILDS
  it: `publish-site.yml` builds AND publishes on every push to `main` (the
  top-bar badge reflected `09343fb0` minutes after that push on
  2026-09-02, which is the measurement); `freeze-app.yml`, `release-tag.yml`,
  `release-notes.yml` and `withdraw-release.yml` are `workflow_dispatch` and
  cover the release chores — `RELEASING.md` has the table.  This paragraph
  used to say the workflow "publishes nothing" and that publishing was a hand
  act; that was true once and had been false for weeks.  **The top-bar
  badge (`Choupo-dev · <commit>`) is the staleness check** — if it is not the
  commit you pushed, the deploy did not land.
- **Health:** run `bin/runTests` — it prints the verdict, and a verdict copied
  into prose is a verdict that drifts.  This line used to read "299 / 0" and
  the suite had been at 344 / 0 for a while.
- **Scale:** **do not read a count from here.**  The single source of truth is
  `bin/curate/release_inventory.py` → `generated/releaseInventory.json`
  (components, species, pair catalogues, unit-op models, runnable cases), and a
  `runTests` gate fails when it goes stale.  CLAUDE.md §6 already says the
  tally must not be hand-maintained "and that includes HERE" — this file was
  carrying its own copy anyway (288 tutorials against 306 in the generated
  inventory), which is the arity sin in the very document that warns about it.

## 2. The architecture in one page (pointers, not a re-derivation)

The authority is [`docs/architecture/CHOUPO-CONSTITUTION.md`](docs/architecture/CHOUPO-CONSTITUTION.md)
(level 1) + [`docs/architecture/property-architecture.md`](docs/architecture/property-architecture.md)
(level 2); the authority map is `docs/architecture/README.md`.  **These were
synchronised with the v2-native engine on 2026-07-23** — they no longer describe
the retired v1 grammar (that catch-up was the point of the last work session).

- **Files on disk are the single source of truth.**  Topology, state, numerics
  and thermodynamics each live in their OWN file; every role is INFERRED, never
  re-declared.  No backward-compatibility shims.
- **A case:** `system/` (controlDict, flowsheetDict = TOPOLOGY only, solverDict,
  outerDict, postDict) · `constant/` (thermoPhysPropDict + propertyManifest +
  records) · `0/` (complete initial stream state, one file per stream).
- **Thermo (v2, NATIVE):** `constant/thermoPhysPropDict`
  (`recordType thermophysicalPropertySystem; schemaVersion 2;`).  The builder
  assembles each `equilibrium.formulation` natively — `gammaPhi`, `gammaGamma`
  (LLE/VLLE), `diluteSolution` (Henry), `phiPhi` (one cubic both roots),
  `electrolyteGammaPhi`.  v1 (`propertyDict`/`thermoPackage`) is REFUSED.
  Author-facing detail: `docs/ai/thermo.md`.
- **Sealing:** `bin/choupo-import` copies a case's dependency closure into its
  own `constant/` under a sha256 `propertyManifest` (`sealed true;` = runs with
  `data/standards/` hidden — the thesis-archive test).
- **Conservation is the curriculum** (the 2607 signature): every converged
  steady run emits a plant-boundary ELEMENT balance by default; batch carries
  material+energy ledgers as exact state differences on the elements datum;
  ctrl integrates an accepted-state ledger.  Claims are tri-state
  (FULL/PARTIAL/UNAVAILABLE) with named reasons, never silent zeros.
- **Engine:** 3 layers (OuterDriver / simulator core / PostProcessor), 4
  binaries by problem class.  UnitOperation base: override `type()` + `solve()`,
  optionally `kpis()`/`producedStreams()`/`profile()`; explicit factory, no
  auto-registration.  All solvers hand-written (Newton-on-tears recycle,
  Wegstein, Nelder-Mead/SQP, RK4/Rosenbrock, Michelsen TPD).  C++17, no external
  libs, Make.

## 3. Settled — do NOT reopen

The standing list is `CLAUDE.md` §5/§10 + the Constitution §7.  The load-bearing
ones for day-to-day work:

- v1 property grammar is DEAD (refusal only); `components/` FLAT; pair catalogues
  under `parameters/<MODEL>/`; assets flat with a `kind` field; `streamFaces`/
  `faces{}` naming closed; `streams{}`/`boundary{}` GONE (role inferred).
- One Gibbs surface per phase.  Elements-at-25 °C datum for all formation/reaction
  enthalpy.  No silent crutch (declare → verify → refuse).  H conserved, T the
  model-dependent readout at model boundaries.
- Element-balance seal requires EVERY element to close (anti-cancellation);
  ONE "Element balance" GUI view; ctrl toys are mass-conserving isomerisations.
- No CMake, no external deps, no auto-registration, no Python rewrite.
  GPL-3.0-or-later; *Choupo* is a TalentGround trademark, separate from the code.
- No competitor names in user-facing manuals.  Choupo is an independent,
  self-funded personal project (not an institutional product) — never frame it
  otherwise in any prose.

## 4. Roadmap for the development line (candidate work, priority-ish)

**DEFERRED BY VITOR 2026-09-26 -- a hand-rolled SQP with finite-difference
gradients ("vamos deixar isso para mais tarde").**  A candidate, not a
commission.  The shape is settled enough to write down so it is not re-argued:
BFGS-damped SQP, l1 merit line search, the QP subproblem on the EXISTING
`solver/ActiveSetQP` (the weighted-least-squares reconciler already is a
constrained QP solver), no external library, glass-box announcements for an
infeasible QP, a rejected step, and a finite-difference step below the inner
solver's tolerance -- the last being the noise that makes SQP over a recycled
flowsheet stall, which is the reason it is not offered lightly anywhere.
FIRST STEP when it is taken up: Hock-Schittkowski witnesses (public, known
optima) run on `ActiveSetQP` before any SQP line is written; a gate sabotaged
by hand; students breaking it.  Nothing built.

**SEPTEMBER 2026 — THE ENGINE IS FROZEN, BY DEFAULT (architect, 2026-09-02;
DELEGATE-WITH-DEFAULT under philosophy §4, reversible by one line here).**
Students adopt this month.  Measured before deciding: in the 30 days to
2026-09-02, 848 commits — 369 to `docs/`, 256 to gates, 217 to `src/` — the
apparatus grew faster than the engine it guards; `CLAUDE.md` gained 1678
lines in August; 73 of 97 design records were born that month; the full
suite takes 37 minutes and the ladder (§6a) was broken four times in one
day by the architect himself.  And of 393 runnable cases, FIVE declare
`tier tutorial;` while the four cases the app offers a student as "your
first clicks" declare no tier at all — the learning surface the app
presents and the one the inventory declares are different things.
Gall: a system that works evolved from a simple one that worked; the
working system is the engine and the corpus, and what does not yet work is
what the student MEETS.  So, for September:

1. **No new unit operations.**  Models only on Vítor's order (Chapman-Enskog
   and modified Eucken, 2026-09-06, were).  **Gates are NOT frozen** — this
   line used to say they were, and it was false within four days: measured
   2026-09-06, fifteen gates landed between 09-02 and 09-06, and each one
   saw a defect no case could see (a crystalliser volume in kilomoles, a
   first law the GUI computed for itself, a dryer that made water).  The
   2026-09-04 ruling *never trade a gate for speed* had already settled it,
   and a freeze line that contradicts a ruling is the stale copy.  What IS
   frozen is the apparatus's SHAPE: no new tier, manifest or framework.
   Engine debts (A2 `identity()`, #34, #35, #13) only if a student case
   trips one.
2. **Cure the memory** — this file's §1 (done 2026-09-02), a home for the
   student-walkthrough programme (legs 4–5 have records, 6 is a task
   title, 1–3 are session memory: reconstruct from `git log`, and where
   that fails say so), and a `CLAUDE.md` DIET by demotion: each §6 slice
   narrative already has a design record; the file keeps the invariant
   and the pointer.
3. **Declare the first path** — `tier tutorial;` on the cases a student
   should meet first, chosen by reading `docs/tutorials-catalogue.md`,
   each one driven in the frozen app in a browser and read as the student
   reads it.  The choice is recorded in the controlDicts, which is the
   deliberate act the tier doctrine asks for.
4. **The delivered artefact under the instrument that found everything on
   2026-09-02** — a TOOL, `bin/drive-app` (built the same day; never a gate: it needs a
   browser and a served copy, the Poling precedent), run from
   `RELEASING.md`'s freeze step, reporting requests outside the prefix,
   views that error, hints that lie.
5. **The last week is empty**, reserved for what students send back.
   The mode of failure of a complex system is not predictable from its
   structure.

**AUTHORISED 2026-09-08 (Vitor: "Sim.  Faz no sabado") -- WHAT MAKES A FOLDER
A LEVEL OF A CASE HAS TWO ANSWERS, AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS DECLARED.**  The
engine reads `sectors ( ... )` / `units ( ... )` from the parent's
flowsheetDict; the GUI indexes a sub-node ONLY when the folder carries its own
`.cho` (`subNodesFor`: `if (!rel.endsWith(".cho")) continue`), and
`drillableSub` then asks `tutorialByName` for it.  A case can therefore be
CORRECT for the engine and MUTE for the GUI, with nothing anywhere saying so:
`greenAmmoniaIndustrialN2` shipped with the root marker alone, and its 4
sectors and 19 unit folders were unreachable by double click while
`bin/runTests`, `--fast` and `--gui` were all green (fixed 2026-09-08 by adding
the 23 markers -- the symptom, not the cause).

Vitor's instinct was "create the `.cho` automatically".  MEASURED, that is the
weak form of the right idea, for two reasons: the marker is no longer empty (it
carries the canvas LAYOUT snapshot, `FlowCanvas.tsx` -- and a drilled sector
becomes its own case, so its marker acquires its own layout), so it cannot
simply be dropped; and whichever TOOL creates it, a case authored by hand and
never passed through that tool stays mute -- the same defect moved, and still
two readers with two answers.

THE SHAPE TO BUILD: the GUI index stops REQUIRING the file to consider a folder
drillable -- it derives membership from the parent's DECLARATION, which is the
one home -- and the `.cho` is written when there is a layout to store, which is
the only thing it stores.  Then the file cannot be missing, because it is no
longer the condition of existence, and a student never has to know it exists.
Plus the gate nothing asserts today: a folder the engine flattens as a member
is openable in the GUI.  Cost, stated: `subNodesFor` gets its list free from
the file map today; deriving means reading each level's `sectors`/`units`
recursively (the GUI has the parser).  The 23 markers already committed stay
correct under either design.

> **2026-08-14 — ONE ITEM IS OPEN.  V1: the lumped-Cp column energy model.**
>
> `Absorber` and `Stripper` share the textbook stage energy balance -- liquid
> Cp is the SOLVENT's alone, vapour Cp is the FEED gas at feed composition,
> both constant across the column, source = heat of absorption.  It does not
> conserve the canonical (formation-datum, full-mixture, T-dependent) enthalpy
> the energy report prices, so every non-isothermal column leaves a first-law
> residual on its own streams: **+82.93 kW** on `absorber01_NH3_water`,
> **-19.87 kW** on `stripper01_NH3_water`, **-11.25 kW** on the acetone
> plant's absorber.
>
> All three were invisible until 2026-08-14, reading `n/a` in the
> model-boundary ledger because the audit only ran on units declaring a duty
> and all three are adiabatic.  The units now ANNOUNCE the approximation (the
> `dynamicCSTR` posture) and the size stays where the report publishes it.
> **Nothing is broken and nothing is waiting on this to keep working.**
>
> THE QUESTION: should the balance be reformulated onto canonical enthalpy?
> It is a PHYSICS change, not a reporting one -- it moves the temperature
> profile, hence the K-values, hence every product composition in every
> absorber and stripper case, including the acetone plant's offgas loss.
>
> **V2 (found the same day, NOT fixed): the energy report prices an UNPINNED
> stream on `vf == 0`, which the constitution bans by name.**
>
> `StreamStateIO`'s reader says it outright: the `vaporFraction` default of
> 0.0 is "a starting value", "reading it as liquid is precisely the implicit
> pin the constitution bans and the flash19 duty was paying for", and
> **"consumers that price energy ask `phasePinned`, never `vf == 0`"**.
> `BalanceMath::streamH_elements` asks `s.vf`: when a stream resolves
> SINGLE-PHASE, `streamSplit` returns nothing and the fallback prices on the
> carried default, so an unpinned vapour is priced as a LIQUID.
>
> Measured on `absorber01_NH3_water`: its gas feed moves from -6572 to
> -4594 J/mol (-182.56 to -127.61 kW) and the column's imbalance from
> +82.93 kW to +27.98 kW.  **That is the ONE confirmed instance.**
>
> `evapDryer01_nacl` was recorded here as a second and is NOT one: its energy
> row is `gap` -- the unit has no elements-datum route, so the report never
> prices its streams and the mispricing cannot occur.  Its `vf 0` is the
> carried default being DISPLAYED, which says nothing about any computation.
>
> A scan finds 27 boundary inlets carrying the signature (unpinned, permanent
> gas plus a sub-critical species), but it cannot separate them, and the two
> examined most closely turned out NOT to be instances.
>
> **THE SCOPE IS NARROWER THAN THE SCAN, and the three cases separate
> cleanly** (checked 2026-08-14, one representative each):
>
> * **SINGLE-PHASE VAPOUR, unpinned, holding a sub-critical species -- the
>   defect.**  `streamSplit` returns nothing (a single-phase resolution is
>   not a split), the fallback prices on `vf == 0`, and a vapour becomes a
>   liquid.  absorber01, evapDryer01.
> * **TWO-PHASE -- not affected.**  `streamSplit` resolves it and prices on
>   the split; only the DISPLAYED `vf` is the carried default.  `flash10`'s
>   feed is genuinely 64 % vapour (the flash runs at the feed's own T and
>   returns V/F 0.6408) and displays `vf 0`, yet its node closes at
>   -2.4e-5 kW with or without a quality pin: the pin shifts every stream's
>   enthalpy together, so it perturbs a correct reading rather than repairing
>   a wrong one.  Cosmetic -- worth knowing before anyone "fixes" 27 files.
> * **ALL components above their Tc -- not affected.**  The Tc screen recovers
>   `vf 1`; the gas-solid feeds (N2 + silica, the solid on its own block)
>   price as vapour correctly.
>
> So the ones that MATTER are those resolving single-phase vapour with a
> sub-critical component present.  ONE is confirmed; the rest are
> unclassified, and the scan cannot separate them without resolving each.
>
> **A DETECTOR WAS BUILT AND WITHDRAWN, and its false positives are worth
> more than its true one.**  An advisory in `streamH_elements` -- fire when an
> UNPINNED stream is about to be priced on `vf == 0` while its own
> equilibrium resolves all-vapour -- was written, built, run over 80 steady
> cases, and REVERTED unshipped.  It cannot make the distinction the
> constitution makes: `phasePinned` is set BY THE FILE READER ONLY, so a
> liquid a UNIT computed is indistinguishable from a file's untouched
> default, and `ProcessStream` says exactly that ("a vf a producing unit
> wrote is not a constraint: it is that unit's answer").
>
> What it flagged was almost entirely COLUMN DISTILLATES -- `column01`, `03`,
> `04`, `05`, `09`, `10`, `12`, `shortcut01`, `acetone05/06/07`, `dewT01`.  A
> total condenser sets `vf = 0` ("already condensed") and the package, handed
> that stream's own (T, P, z), answers ALL VAPOUR.  Either those distillates
> are reported at a state that is not a liquid, or the package and the column
> disagree about the same point -- the column/thermo version of the
> absorber's lumped-Cp gap.  ONE CASE SETTLED IT -- see V3.

> **V3 (2026-08-14): the distillate is reported at the overhead's DEW point
> while labelled a fully condensed liquid.**
>
> `column01_benzene_toluene`, measured with the engine's own saturation units
> on the distillate's own composition (98.12 % benzene / 1.88 % toluene,
> 1 atm):
>
> | | K |
> |---|---|
> | `T_bubble` (`bubbleT` unit) | 353.6310 |
> | `T_dew` (`dewT` unit) | **354.2132** |
> | what the column reports for `distillate` | **354.211**, `vf = 0` |
>
> The reported temperature coincides with the DEW point to 0.002 K and sits
> 0.58 K above the bubble point.  `DistillationColumn.cpp` sets
> `dStream.T = T[0]` with `dStream.vf = 0.0; // already condensed`, and the
> condenser duty is a latent heat evaluated isothermally at that same `T[0]`.
> A total condenser's saturated liquid product is at the BUBBLE point of
> `xD`; the dew point is where condensation BEGINS.
>
> WHAT IS MEASURED: the three temperatures above, and that the same shape
> appears on every column the withdrawn detector reached (`column01`, `03`,
> `04`, `05`, `09`, `10`, `12`, `shortcut01`, `acetone05/06/07`, `dewT01`).
> WHAT IS **NOT** ESTABLISHED, and I am not asserting it: whether `T[0]`
> being the dew point is a deliberate isothermal-condenser convention that
> the duty term is consistent with, or an error in the stage-0 temperature.
> The two have different fixes and I have run out of evidence, not out of
> arithmetic.
>
> THE STAKE: 0.58 K on this narrow-boiling binary, and the gap widens with
> the boiling range.  Any fix moves ~12 column goldens and the acetone plant,
> so it is yours.  It also decides whether the withdrawn V2 detector was
> reporting a defect or a convention when it flagged those distillates.
>
> **V4 (2026-08-15, found by the fleet sweep): the fractal cascade hands a
> child the DICT but not the DATA HOME the dict's model needs.**
> `twoSectorDemo`'s dignified children (SECTOR_R/S) inherit the parent's

>
> Both cases tested are REPORTING-only: their unit models carry their own Cp

>
> THE QUESTION: should `streamH_elements` price an unpinned single-phase
> stream on its RESOLVED phase instead of the carried default?  The reader's
> own contract says yes; the risk is that every mispriced stream's reported

6. ~~**A6 cyclic steady state (adsorption)**~~ — **BUILT 2026-08-02** on
   Vítor's "faz como achares melhor / Avança!".  `cycle { period; repeat;
   steps ( … ); cssTolerance }` expands to the SAME event stream the
   hand-unrolled recipe produced — proven on all 51 KPIs of batch23's
   golden, which is what let its hand-written list be retired.  The trap
   the design had missed and the build caught: a unit's packed state also
   holds MONOTONE ACCUMULATORS (the bed's M_in/M_out and Q_wall rows),
   which grow every cycle by construction — comparing the whole vector
   would report a perfectly cyclic bed as never settling, so
   `cycleState()` is a virtual each unit overrides to return only what
   repeats (the bed cuts at `inOffset_()`, the layout's own boundary).
   The verdict is tri-state — CONVERGED / NOT-YET with the measured
   change / UNAVAILABLE, with two distinct named reasons for the last
   (fewer than two boundaries, or no declared tolerance) — and the
   engine NEVER invents the tolerance: whether a bed has converged is a
   modelling judgement.  Gate `check_cycle_css` (equivalence + 4
   refusals), sabotage-verified: dropping the k·period offset breaks
   equivalence by 7e-1.  Stop-at-CSS (`repeat untilCSS;`) stays the
   named next step.  Originally designed 2026-08-01,
   [`docs/design/fixed-bed-thermal-a5.md`](docs/design/fixed-bed-thermal-a5.md) §7:
   a `cycle { period; steps (…); repeat N; }` recipe grammar +
   per-cycle state snapshots + a tri-state CSS verdict against a
   tolerance the CASE declares.  It touches the recipe grammar EVERY
   batch case reads, which is why it is yours.  `batch23_tsa_cycles`
   already MEASURES the approach it cannot claim (qbar 0.315 → 0.242 →
   0.175 over three cycles).

> **C201 ITEM 1, MEASURED, AND NOT LANDED (the architect, 2026-11-02).**
> Cause confirmed in the code: the liquid acetic acid is the monomer
> ideal-gas datum minus a Watson latent heat scaled from `HvapTb 24390`,
> which is the heat to the DIMERISED vapour (Component.cpp h_formation,
> liquid rung); the cstr01 reaction heat -25.7 kJ/mol is that 24 kJ/mol.
> A general derived the bridge from the curated vapour dimerisation (one
> parser, no copied constants): acetic liquid -486.3 vs -484.3, reaction
> heat -0.38 kJ/mol at 298 K against about -3 measured.  Branch
> `backup/c201-acetic-bridge` (49a16f684), moved-row list
> `c201-item1-moved-rows.md` in docs/design on that branch.  **Not merged,
> because it trades one error for another:** (a) 182 rows in 14 cases price
> acetic acid's vaporisation to the ideal-gas MONOMER in units whose vapour
> model has no dimer, so for a real dimerised vapour the duties become too
> large (aceticAcid02_plant lights condenser -36.5 -> -75.1 kW, column05
> reboiler +33 %); the other half is the vapour side of
> `docs/design/one-record-two-vapours-acetic-acid.md` (association as a
> property of the VAPOUR model), which must land WITH the bridge, as one

> **DECIDED (the architect, 2026-11-02; this takes the two questions

> (i) `HvapTb` speaks the MEASURED latent heat, to the real associated

> one flash formulation: wherever a component carries a curated vapour
> association (today acetic acid's `vapourDimerisation`, read by ONE parser,
> `thermo/VapourAssociation.H` on the bridge branch), an ideal-gas vapour is
> the equilibrium monomer + dimer mixture (the chemical theory of vapour
> imperfection) -- its fugacity is the MONOMER partial pressure, so the pure
> limit stays exact (p_m + p_d = the record's apparent Psat, and the liquid
> side uses the monomer's saturation pressure solved from the same K), and
> its enthalpy carries the association heat.  ONE home, extracted from the
> reactive VLE builder (`SpeciationSolver`, the v = t_mono + 2 t_dim
> re-weighting), reached through `ThermoPackage`'s K-values and vapour
> enthalpy, so every unit sees it; the liquid bridge (piece 1) lands IN THE
> SAME SLICE.  An equation-of-state vapour carrying an associating component
> keeps its EoS and ANNOUNCES that the association is not priced (no silent
> double treatment).  Validation before landing: a non-reactive acetic
> acid + water T-x-y against a measured dataset the tree can cite, the
> pure-component limit, and the cstr01 reaction heat within the bridge

> **C201 ITEM 1, THE VAPOUR HALF BUILT AND NOT LANDED (2026-11-02).**  Branch
> `backup/c201-acetic-vapour` (1bdfda51f = the bridge branch merged with main
> plus the associated vapour): one home in `thermo/VapourAssociation.H`, read
> by `ThermoPackage` K / Kvec / H_real / S_real, the reactive builder, the
> isothermal flash, the column's vapour-dependence test, the bubble point and
> three property ops (the dimer heat is now counted once; flash13's unit
> residual -0.25 -> 0).  Measured: the pure limit holds (boils at 391.0085 K
> for a record Tb of 391.05); acetic acid + water at 1 atm against Calvar et
> al. 2005 (24 points, located through the ThermoML toolchain) improves,
> T 3.49 -> 2.19 K, y_water 0.0355 -> 0.0272; cstr01's reaction heat stays in
> the reference band.  **Not landed, for four reasons:** (1) **the engine
> prices 33.03 kJ/mol between saturated liquid and saturated vapour at Tb,
> against the record's measured 24.39 (+35 %)**, so the lights condenser of
> aceticAcid02_plant comes back to -52.1 kW (golden -36.5, bridge alone
> -75.1) instead of its old value: the record's inputs do not agree with each
> other at Tb (Watson applied to the APPARENT latent heat, the constant
> liquid Cp, the dimerisation constant extrapolated 93 K); a hypothesis to
> TEST, not a decision: Watson should extrapolate the monomer-basis latent
> heat (HvapTb + dimer fraction x dimer heat at Tb), not the apparent one;
> (2) `check_energy_closure` fails on aceticAcid02_plant (+8.69 kW): the
> column publishes a distillate with 7 % CO on its own dew point, so the
> report's re-flash picks the side by the last digits -- the fix belongs to
> the column (partial condenser or a vent), not to this slice; (3) readers
> still on a monomer ideal gas: the Gibbs reactors (GibbsMethod, DirectMin,
> EquilibriumReactor), `VaporPhase::fEffective` and `binaryTxy` in
> SaturationCurves; (4) the association record is matched by formula
> (C2H4O2), so methylFormate would be taken for acetic acid -- an identity
> decision.  741 rows move over the 37 acetic-acid cases (grouped list in
> that branch's moved-rows doc); the content decision on the seven
> exotherm tutorials is unchanged.  NEXT, in Opus: settle (1) by testing the
> hypothesis against the NBS liquid, then (2)-(4).
> **The hypothesis tested by hand (the architect, 2026-11-02, the record's
> own numbers; arithmetic reproduced the general's 32.99 kJ/mol to 0.04):**
> Watson on the MONOMER-basis latent heat gives 26.17 kJ/mol at Tb (+7 %
> against 24.39) but puts the 298 K liquid at -479.6 kJ/mol against NBS's
> -484.5 (4.9 kJ/mol high).  Decisive control: pinning the 298 K liquid to
> NBS itself still prices 31.11 kJ/mol at Tb.  So the contradiction is NOT
> Watson's: with this record's liquid Cp (123.1, constant) and dimerisation
> (log K25 2.555 bar^-1, dH -63.18 kJ/mol, van 't Hoff with constant dH over
> 93 K) the NBS liquid at 298 K and the measured latent heat at Tb are
> 6.7 kJ/mol apart.  A rising liquid Cp (~150 J/mol K near Tb, unverified)
> accounts for ~1 kJ/mol of it; the rest sits in the vapour's association at
> Tb (the dimer share needed is ~0.37 mol dimer per mol vaporised against
> the 0.26 the record's K gives there).  NEXT is a READING, not code: Chao &
> Zwolinski 1978 (the record's own primary, srd.nist.gov reprint) for the
> dimerisation's temperature dependence and the equilibrium-mixture latent
> heat they tabulate, and a primary liquid Cp(T); only then which anchor the
> slice honours.
> **Lesson recorded:** a data-record chain (datum, latent heat, Cp, K, dH)
> that is individually cited can still be jointly inconsistent; check the
> closure of the chain (latent heat at Tb) before building an engine home on
> it.

> **C218 / C219 / C220 (Vitor, 2026-11-04).**  C218 (EduTool): why a reaction
> is "reversible" or "irreversible", and when quenching works.  Findings
> recorded: no reaction is irreversible (microscopic reversibility, K =
> k_f/k_r = exp(-DeltaG/RT)); "irreversible" means K large enough at THESE
> conditions, and it changes with temperature; "irreversible" collides with
> the thermodynamic sense (entropy production) -- the root of a common
> confusion; quenching is kinetic trapping and applies to ENDOTHERMIC,
> metastable products (steam cracking, NO, acetylene), is NOT universal (the
> exothermic reversible ones want the lowest T with a rate: ammonia, methanol,
> SO3) and "quench" also names a cold-shot that moves along the equilibrium
> curve, which is a different act.  The page computes K(T) and the
> equilibrium conversion from the catalogue (ethane, ethylene, acetylene and
> NO carry formation data), overlays a declared rate and a cooling rate and
> shows the freezing temperature (cooling time RT^2/E against 1/k).  C219:
> liquid-liquid extraction COLUMNS: the engine has the countercurrent
> cascade of equilibrium stages (`extractor`, an LL flash per stage, two
> tutorials) but not the equipment -- no packed, rotating-disc, pulsed or
> mixer-settler model, no HETS, no flooding or diameter, no stage efficiency;
> steps: (1) a declared stage efficiency as the distillation has, (2) sizing
> by a DECLARED HETS with its source, (3) flooding and diameter only on a
> readable source with a worked example (Treybal, Perry's, Seader, or Lo,
> Baird & Hanson) -- Vitor supplies the books.  C220 (WAITS, "para mais
> tarde"): a RARE-EARTH separation case, if the data can be taken from the
> open literature.  State of the ground: lithium has the sectored brine plant
> (Pitzer, NRTL LLE, carbonation, hot air, finishing) and wants solar
> evaporation ponds and direct extraction; rare earths have NO lanthanide in
> the catalogue, and the separation is mass-action solvent extraction (D2EHPA
> / PC88A) in cascades of hundreds of stages with adjacent separation factors
> of only 1.5 to 3, which the Gibbs-minimising LL flash with an activity model
> cannot represent -- it needs a reactive extraction with one equilibrium
> constant per element and its pH and extractant dependence, and those
> constants live in scattered, partly paywalled papers that disagree.  Order:
> an EduTool first (why a factor of 1.5 needs so many stages, from a two-
> component Kremser-type count, no data needed), then a research general for
> ONE open-access separation (Nd/Pr or Dy/Tb) with printed constants and
> cascade, and only then the mass-action extractor.
>
> **C219 phase 1, BUILT (2026-11-04, branch c219; Perry's 9th ed. Sec. 15
> and Treybal Ch. 10, numbers only).**  (A) `op:lleTieLines` +

> **C222 (Vitor, 2026-11-04): AN EDUTOOL ON WHY THE TRANSFER UNIT WAS INVENTED
> ("porque raio inventaram a unidade de transferencia ... nunca ninguem me
> explicou bem").**  Sources now local and readable: Treybal, *Mass-Transfer
> Operations* 3rd ed. (Ch. 7 defines N_tG and H_tG, Eqs 7.59-7.60, and ties
> them to the Murphree efficiency E = 1 - exp(-N_tG) for constant-equilibrium
> contacting; Ch. 8 Fig. 8.20 and the absorber NTU; Ch. 10 Illustration 10.10
> for liquid extraction), Perry's 9th ed. Sec. 15 Example 15-3 (NTU for an
> extractor) and its HTU/HETS tables; the origin cited by Treybal for the
> concept is Chilton & Colburn, Ind. Eng. Chem. 27, 255 (1935) (to be read
> before the page names it).  The lesson, in one line: Z = H x N -- the
> integral of dy/(y - y*) is the DIFFICULTY of the separation (equilibrium
> and material balance only, independent of the packing) and H = G/(K a) is
> what the EQUIPMENT delivers per unit of difficulty (mass transfer and
> hydrodynamics only, independent of the separation): a continuous contactor
> has no stages to count.  The page: the differential balance, the two
> numbers drawn apart, N for a straight operating and equilibrium line in
> closed form and for a curved one by quadrature of the ENGINE's own
> equilibrium (no physics in TS: the curve arrives from the engine run), the
> relation to the equilibrium stage (HETS = H_OG ln(A)/(A-1) for straight
> lines) and to the stage efficiency, and the worked example of Perry's 15-3
> and Treybal's 10.10 reproduced.  When: after C219's first phase (the
> `extractor` validated against Perry's Table 15-8), so the page can end on
> a column the engine ran.

> **C226 MEASURED (2026-11-05, Vitor: "resolve ja a questao do jacobiano"):
> THE FITTING JACOBIAN IS NOT A PROBLEM; NOTHING ANALYTIC IS BUILT.**  Two
> measurements on the curation cases, run from the shipped binary.  SPEED:
> `curate04` (methanol-water, 54 points, 7 iterations) takes 0.12 s,
> `curate12` 0.08 s, `curate02` (29 iterations) 0.05 s; extrapolated to 269
> points it is below one second, so the analytic Jacobian and the parallel
> points that C226 A4 proposed would buy nothing a student or an assistant
> could feel.  ACCURACY OF THE IDENTIFIABILITY: the third `curate04` fit is
> the ill-conditioned one (four parameters, cond(JtJ) about 1.4e9); varying
> its `fdStep` over six decades (1e-2 ... 1e-7) leaves the verdict "NOT
> individually identifiable" unchanged every time, the condition number
> between 1.23e9 and 1.36e9, and b_ij between -1652 and -1687; the shipped
> 1e-4 is within 0.002 % of the h -> 0 limit (-1686.63 against -1686.98),
> and only the coarsest step, 1e-2, moves a parameter by 2 %.  So the finite
> difference noise does not decide any verdict and the argument for the
> analytic form that C226 recorded as stronger than speed is NOT borne out.
> What C226 A4 should have named instead is where a chain of fits spends its
> time: the CAS -> InChIKey `identity` step (minutes, network), not the
> fit.  Reopen the analytic Jacobian only if a fit of a different kind (the
> liquid-liquid residual, thousands of points) measures slow.  CHECKED THE SAME DAY (Vitor: "verifica se esse caso e lento primeiro"):
> the liquid-liquid residual does not exist yet, so what was measured is its
> unit cost.  A BINARY liquid-liquid flash (`binary01_lle_water_nbutanol`,
> a 41-node grid plus both binodal points) runs under the 10 ms resolution
> of `time` (three runs, 0.00 s), i.e. as cheap as a bubble point; at 78
> butanol-water points and five evaluations per Jacobian that is at most
> seconds per iteration, so the binary pairs this chain is for are NOT slow.
> The slow LL path is the TERNARY scan (`ternary03_lle_water_ethanol_
> benzene`: 105 nodes, 21 tie lines, 6.6 s), which no pair fit uses.  If the
> residual is later built on `IsothermalFlash::solveCore` (the
> multi-start Nelder-Mead path) instead of the binary common-tangent
> solution, that cost changes by orders of magnitude -- MEASURED the same
> day and FALSE: a sweep of `vlle01_waterButanol`'s decanter, a binary
> liquid-liquid flash through `IsothermalFlash::solveCore` (the multi-start
> path) at every point, takes 0.01 s for 2 points, 0.03 s for 40 and 0.29 s
> for 400, i.e. LINEAR at about 0.7 ms per flash; with the feed moved OUT of

> take 0.23 s.  At 78 points and five evaluations per Jacobian that is about

> Vitor: "ate fiquei envergonhado ... as ligacoes dos tubos aos equipamentos
> estao muito mais precisas!".  MEASURED, and he is right:
> `PlantLayout.cpp:705-712` sends EVERY pipe into and out of an item at its
> PLAN CENTRE, AT ITS TOP ("Stylised: no nozzle schedule is published by any
> sizer"), so a column's feed, reflux and bottoms all meet at one point on
> the head; a stream with several consumers is not routed at all
> (`PlantLayout.cpp:812-826`); `equipmentModel.ts` draws nozzles as decoration
> and exposes no port.  The viewer (`layoutRenderer.ts`) has orbit, phase
> colours, quality levels, tooltips and particles, and NO tour, walk or
> drone camera, go-to list, temperature colour, minimap or click card.  What
> the page cannot do and Choupo does: it is authored for ONE plant, its own
> legend says the dimensions are indicative and the routing "not modelled",
> and nothing checks it; Choupo's is generated from any case and checked
> (separations, zones, roads, pipe clashes).  So the target is the union, not
> a defence.  DECISIONS (architect, rule 00): (A) THE ENGINE PUBLISHES PORTS:
> each pipe end lands on a port derived from the item's kind, its sized
> dimensions and the stream's ROLE (a column: feed at its stage's height,
> vapour at the head, bottoms at the sump; an exchanger: shell and tube
> in/out; a drum: inlet on the side, vapour on top, liquid at the bottom; a
> compressor or pump: suction and discharge), with a case override, and
> ANNOUNCED as a conventional position, not a vendor's nozzle schedule; the
> `layout` golden rows of pipe length move, listed in the commit.  (B) THE
> VIEWER gains the guided tour (generated from the sectors and units, never
> hand-written per plant), orbit/walk/drone, go-to, colour by phase,
> temperature, pressure and the CONCENTRATION of a chosen component (Vitor: the
> students' page does this too; every value read from the published stream,
> never computed in the GUI), the minimap, and a click card reading the stream

> **C231 DESIGN (architect, 2026-11-06, Vitor: "faz o que for preciso ... de
> forma elegante").**  Read first: the extent machinery lives in the CMO MESH
> (`solveSimultaneous`, `extentOf`, `xi`, the homotopy on `lnOffset`), the
> variable flows and the stage energy rows live in the full MESH (`residualF`),
> and `C169` refuses to join them.  So the column gains no new solver: the FULL
> MESH gains the extents.  (1) One unknown per reactive stage appended to `w`;
> component rows `-= nu[i]*xi_j`; TOTAL rows `-= sumNu*xi_j` (the whole of the
> mole change); no heat term at all, because the energy rows price on the
> elements datum and the heat of reaction is ALREADY there -- adding one would
> count it twice; the equilibrium row is the CMO's `lnQ - ln K_a(T)`.  (2)
> K_a(T) FROM THE RECORDS, the elegant half: `equilibrium { fromRecords; }`
> gives ln K_a(T) = -Sum nu_i [g_ig,i(T)/(RT) + ln(Psat_i(T)/P0)], the same
> datum that prices the energy rows, so a column cannot carry one heat of
> reaction in its K and another in its energy balance; `equilibrium { lnKa
> "<formula>"; ... }` through `core/Formula` (the C67 rule: a law WRITTEN in the
> case, parsed once, dimension-checked) is the cited alternative; `Ka298` +
> `dHrxn` stay for the CMO esterifications, byte-identical.  (3) The source
> case's specs are BOTTOMS RATE and BOILUP RATIO (240 kmol/h, 5), and with a
> mole change D is no longer F - B, so the MESH gains that spec pair, D
> becoming an unknown closed by the top balance; `refluxRatio` +
> `distillateRate` keep their rows, with B = F + sumNu Sum xi - D.  (4) The
> seed is announced: a NON-REACTIVE CMO seeds the full MESH, and the reaction
> enters by the existing homotopy (no silent crutch).  (5) `model simultaneous`
> keeps refusing Sum nu != 0 by name and now names `fullMESH`.  THE DATA ARE THE
> REAL RISK, not the solver: isobutene's `dHf_298` and `dGf_298` are JOBACK
> estimates (`data/standards/components/isoButene.dat`, origin estimated), so
> K_a(T) fromRecords and the heat of reaction inherit that error, announced.
> The cure is a primary datum (a citable isobutene enthalpy of formation) and a
> measured K_a(T) of the MTBE reaction to hold the result against; a value is
> NEVER read off the source case's results.  Non-reactive columns must be
> byte-identical (every golden unmoved).

> **C231 DATA, READ (2026-11-06).**  K_a(T) of methanol + isobutene <-> MTBE:
> Izquierdo, Cunill, Vila, Tejero, Iborra, J. Chem. Eng. Data 37 (1992) 339-343,
> doi 10.1021/je00007a019 (in `~/Choupo-Literature/`), measured at 313-353 K, in
> activities with UNIFAC.  THE PRINTED EQ. 16 IS UNUSABLE: its rounded constant
> gives K about 7 times BELOW the paper's own Table IV (16 against 118 at 40 C;
> checked, not assumed), and its Eq. 19 runs 19 % high.  Eq. 15, dH = -39.1
> kJ/mol and dS = -85.3 J/mol/K, reproduces the 21 measurements of its Table II
> at an AAD of 4.6 % (max 8.5 %), so that is the K of the witness.  Isobutene:
> the catalogue's `dHf_298` is a Joback estimate, -10.25 kJ/mol, which puts the
> gas-phase heat of reaction at -72.3 kJ/mol against the paper's -65.4.
> Prosen, Maron, Rossini, J. Res. NBS 46 (1951) 106, doi 10.6028/jres.046.015,
> give the heat of combustion, 645.19 +/- 0.25 kcal/mol, hence about -17.9 +/-
> 1.1 kJ/mol with CODATA CO2 and H2O; used as a case-local overlay in the
> witness, the catalogue record to be corrected in its own curation act (three
> cases name it).

> **C231 PAPERS READ (2026-11-06): NONE OF THE FOUR VALIDATES THE COLUMN.**
> Mohl, Kienle, Gilles, Chem. Eng. Sci. 54 (1999) 1029 (doi 10.1016/s0009-2509(98)
> 00327-3): two Clausthal pilot columns, MTBE and TAME, but its experimental
> verification is TAME-centred and in FIGURES (3, 7), no tables; packed and
> kinetic.  Sundmacher & Hoffmann, Chem. Eng. Sci. 51 (1996) 2359 (doi
> 10.1016/0009-2509(96)00092-9): a laboratory MTBE column, but a NONEQUILIBRIUM
> model with kinetics and intraparticle diffusion, comparisons in figures (8).
> Nijhuis, Kerkhof, Mak, Ind. Eng. Chem. Res. 32 (1993) 2767 (doi
> 10.1021/ie00023a045): a SIMULATION study run in the commercial package itself,
> kinetic.  Jacobs & Krishna, Ind. Eng. Chem. Res. 32 (1993) 1706 (doi
> 10.1021/ie00020a025): simulation.  The Mohl paper was chosen from its title; the
> reading corrected that.  WHAT THE CASE MAY CLAIM: the thermodynamics is
> validated (K_a(T) against Izquierdo's 21 measurements, AAD 4.6 %); the column is
> verified against the reference simulator (temperatures within 0.3 K, duties 8 %
> high, cause not investigated), which is agreement and not truth.  A real
> column-level validation needs a KINETIC reactive stage in the full MESH
> (Rehfinger & Hoffmann) and digitised figures with a checked calibration; it is
> the next step of this line, not a task for the freeze.

> **C233 (Vitor, 2026-11-06): KINETICS IN THE FULL MESH.**  "Sera que podes por
> no plano CML implementar cinetica no full MESH?"  Why: C231 refuses `kinetics`
> in `fullMESH` by name, and without it the MTBE column cannot be held against a
> pilot column (C231 papers read: none of the four validates it).  Scope, from
> what the code already carries: the CMO MESH has a kinetic mode
> (`kinetic`, `rateAt`, `mCatPerStage`, `pseudoHomogeneous` and `adsorption`)
> whose extent is COMPUTED from the rate and the catalyst mass of the stage, not
> an unknown; the full MESH takes it the same way (extent per reactive stage =
> r x m_cat), through the reaction factory (`Arrhenius`, `LHHW`, `expression`,
> DEV.md C67) so a rate law's numbers live in the case, not in `src/`.  The
> law to hold it against is Rehfinger & Hoffmann, Chem. Eng. Sci. 45 (1990) 1605,
> doi 10.1016/0009-2509(90)80013-5 (rate in liquid-phase ACTIVITIES, in
> `~/Choupo-Literature/`).  KEEP APART, said in the case: the pilot columns
> (Mohl; Sundmacher & Hoffmann) are packed, catalyst-particle-limited columns;
> a pseudo-homogeneous stage rate does not carry intraparticle diffusion
> (the effectiveness factor), so the first witness must be a configuration where
> that is plausible, and the comparison is announced as approximate.  ORDER:
> design with Opus (how the computed extent enters the Newton and its
> Jacobian, and the homotopy), build with Sonnet, then digitise a pilot-column
> profile with a checked calibration.  Needs C231 integrated first.

> **C233 DESIGN (architect, 2026-11-06, Vitor: "comeca ja").**  THE LAW, read
> from the page image of Rehfinger & Hoffmann 1990: r = k [a_IB/a_MeOH - (1/K_a)
> a_MTBE/a_MeOH^2] (Eq. 12), k in mmol/(s eq), k(90 C) = 243.8 +/- 27.0, E = 92.4
> +/- 3.7 kJ/mol (Eq. 15, Table 4), K_a(25 C) = 300.5 +/- 22.8 (Table 4, fitted)
> with ln[K_a(T)/K_a(T0)] = Eq. 6 (A1 = -1.49277e3 K, A2 = -7.74002e1, A3 =
> 5.07563e-1 /K, A4 = -9.12739e-4 /K2, A5 = 1.10649e-6 /K3, A6 = -6.27996e-10
> /K4; T0 298.15 K).  Eq. 6 CHECKED: with K_a(298) = 284 it reproduces the seven
> Rehfinger values of Izquierdo's Table IV exactly.  Activities there are UNIQUAC
> and the rate is per acid EQUIVALENT, so a case declares the resin's capacity.
> THE LAW DOES NOT FIT `rateAt`: forward order -1 in methanol, and a reverse leg
> with a_MeOH^-2 that is not mass action.  So the column takes it through the
> reaction FACTORY (DEV.md C67): `reaction { kinetics { model expression; ... } }`
> read by `ReactionRate::New`, with `a[i]` added to the state the law may read
> (`RateState` gains the activities, `RateOffer` says who supplies them; a reactor
> that does not refuses by name).  The native `pseudoHomogeneous` and `adsorption`
> words stay byte-identical.  In the full MESH the extent is COMPUTED, r(T_j, x_j,
> gamma_j) x m_cat_j, not an unknown (as in the CMO), the catalyst mass entering
> by the existing ramp; the energy rows take nothing, as in C231.  THE GATE THAT
> PROVES IT IS A LIMIT: with a law whose K is the equilibrium witness's K, a
> growing catalyst mass must CONVERGE on column19's equilibrium answer; zero
> catalyst must give the non-reactive column.  KNOWN HAZARD, said in the case: the
> law diverges as a_MeOH -> 0 and the paper warns below x_MeOH about 0.3, while a
> reactive zone runs lean in methanol; a floor, if any, is WRITTEN in the case's
> law (`max(...)`), never hidden in the engine, and the reactive stages' a_MeOH is
> reported against the measured range.  Internal diffusion (the effectiveness
> factor) is NOT modelled and is said so.

> **C235, THE DESIGN BELOW IS RETRACTED (architect, 2026-11-07, the sweep's 102 failures
> sent it back to the physics).  THE LIQUID RUNG WAS RIGHT AND THE IDEAL VAPOUR WAS
> WRONG.**  Kirchhoff from 298 K prices h_ig - h_L, not the latent heat: at 298 K the
> vapour is near ideal, and the liquid's enthalpy has no reason to know about the
> vapour's departure at 401 K.  So h_ig - h_L = 24.14 kJ/mol against a true latent of
> about 22.8 is not an error of the rung: 24.14 - 1.34 (H_res of a Redlich-Kwong vapour
> at 7 bar) = 22.80, on Watson's 22.84 and the source case's 22.92.  The "double count"
> in the correction below does not exist: this rung never subtracted Watson, it was
> read before the code that says so (`speciesPhaseEnthalpy`, "THE STATE IDENTITY #106").
> Commit e149c478e (Watson slope above the window) broke dh/dT == Cp for every reader of
> Cp, moved 102 rows of cases and gates (`check_ctrl_balance`, `check_reference_rung`,
> `check_cp_range_announced`), and matched the source case by putting the vapour's
> error into the liquid.  IT DOES NOT LAND.  The fix is the vapour: `column19` declares
> an EoS as the source case does, with (B) the feed's own pressure, and (A) phi_sat in
> the liquid reference so the temperatures hold.  The window remains a caveat, not a
> defect: the extrapolation is announced.

> **C242 (Vitor, 2026-11-07: "vê online o que tu precisas de fazer e a forma de te
> organizares para gerir um software deste calibre"): THE OPERATING SYSTEM, READ FROM
> THE PRACTICE AND MEASURED AGAINST OURS.**  STATUS: rules adopted below; they enter
> CLAUDE.md section 10 when the C241 diet lands (one writer on that file at a time).
> WHAT WAS READ: Osmani, *The code agent orchestra* ("verification is the bottleneck,
> not generation"; 3-5 agents, 1 reviewer per 3-4 builders, "don't run more agents than
> you can meaningfully review"; one file one owner; plan approved before code; stuck 3+
> iterations on one error -> stop and reassign; hard caps on iterations, time and
> tokens, pause at 85 %; the lead keeps architecture, scope and review, and approves
> every line of the context file -- agent-written context files gave no benefit, ETH
> Zurich); Augment, *multi-agent workspace* (a single-writer rule for hotspot files --
> registries, configs; specs with acceptance criteria; tests plus automated gates before
> every merge, merges sequential; "git detects textual conflicts, not semantic ones");
> CFD Direct on OpenFOAM maintenance (Lehman: growth paced so users, trainers and
> documentation keep up; small frequent changes stable, large infrequent ones not; a
> maintainer needs enough time to stay familiar with the code); OpenFOAM's layered test
> battery (daily units, weekly medium, release-time industrial); Ernst, Kazman & Delange,
> *Technical Debt in Practice* (track it, 7-15 % of the backlog is normal; look beyond
> code to tests and documentation) and arXiv 2603.20415 on SCIENTIFIC debt (a flawed
> physical assumption in code, which code-debt tools miss); the risk-register and
> WIP-limit literature (limits drift upward until they never trigger; a weekly flow
> review).  MEASURED AGAINST CHOUPO: briefs carry measured claims but rarely an explicit
> pass/fail list or an ownership list; the machine budget allows 7 generals and today 6
> ran while integration -- the architect's serial lane -- was the bottleneck (five ready
> branches queued behind one integration); no brief carried a time or token cap (the
> C235 general ran 4.2 h and 736k tokens, well, but unbounded); no independent reviewer
> read a slice before integration; the only hooks are a stop hook; technical debt is
> registered (`debt_registry.py`, KNOWN_OPEN pins) but RISK is not; the full sweep runs
> when a slice forces it, not on a cadence.  RULES ADOPTED (architect, rule 00):
> (1) A BRIEF ENDS WITH `Accepts when:` (3-6 checkable lines) AND `Owns:` / `Does not
> touch:` (paths); a general that must touch a path it does not own stops and asks.
> (2) WIP: at most 4 BUILDERS in flight, and when 3 branches are `queued` for
> integration no new builder starts -- the slot goes to integrating or to a reviewer.
> (3) Every brief carries a BUDGET (wall time, and the largest change allowed: goldens,
> files); the general reports at half and stops at the cap with its state; stuck 3
> rounds on one error -> it stops and reports, with the reflection line "what failed,
> what would fix it, am I repeating myself".  (4) A slice over ~2 h, or touching a shared
> path, starts with a PLAN REPORT (<= 30 lines) the architect approves before code.
> (5) A slice that moves goldens or touches a shared path gets a READ-ONLY REVIEWER
> (brief + acceptance list, fresh context) before integration; its verdict is in the
> commit.  (6) HOTSPOT FILES have one writer, the architect: CLAUDE.md, BRAIN.md,
> DEV.md, PLAN.md; generated views regenerate at integration; `bin/runTests` and the
> registries are edited by one general at a time.  (7) A CADENCE: every Saturday the
> full sweep, the slowest list, the BRAIN rows, the risk table and the Done pruning,
> whether or not a slice forced it; Wednesday a half-week check of the plan's caps.
> (8) A RISK TABLE in BRAIN.md (likelihood, impact, mitigation, review date), scientific
> debt named as a class.  (9) One builder slot in four goes to debt, speed or validation,
> never to a feature.  (10) Checkable rules move to hooks: first `git add -A` and
> `git add .` refused by a PreToolUse hook; then "no edit of `bin/runTests`, `src/` or
> `gui/` while a suite runs".

> **C367 (2026-11-12; the architect's decision, from the Tb-vs-Antoine gate
> red on six components).**  Read against the measured ThermoML points: two
> declared boiling points were wrong and are corrected (diNButylEther 415.35
> -> 414.55 K, measured; squalane 623.15 -> 686.4 K, the article's own
> extrapolated 1-atm entry, said as such -- the same table has 12 kPa at
> 600 K).  For the others the ROOT CAUSE is the fit, not Tb: a
> three-parameter Antoine fitted over the whole measured range
> (methylDiEthanolAmine to 738 K and 3985 kPa) cannot hold both ends, and
> `choupo-curate vp` has no way to restrict it.  DECIDED: the curation gets a
> DECLARED fit window with a mandatory reason, one uniform physical rule
> (never a window chosen to satisfy the gate), `Trange` equal to the window
> fitted, and the error on the points left out printed beside the grade.
> dimethylethanolamine's Tb is contradicted by a measurement (406.80 K at
> 100 kPa) and is set from the two measured points that bracket 1 atm only if
> the origin vocabulary can say "derived from named measurements".
> dimethylsulfoxide is PINNED as debt, not fitted away: ebulliometric normal
> boiling points (median 462.19 K, 11 articles) and boiling points inside

> **C363 (Vitor, 2026-11-12, in the cloud session: "e se tu aqui apenas

> Serias o meu validador!" and, to the conditions the cloud put, "Sim,

> SESSION BUILDS: every engine and GUI slice (units, models, solvers, pages).
> THE CLOUD SESSION (a) PRODUCES CATALOGUE DATA -- components, binary and
> Henry records from the archive it holds, with their curation tools -- and
> (b) VALIDATES what the laptop lands.  The rules of the validation:
> (1) BY MEASUREMENT, NOT BY READING: each review runs the cases, recomputes
> the result by an independent route, sabotages by hand to see whether the
> slice's own gates fire, and compares with measured data where the archive
> or an open source has it; an opinion formed by reading alone is not a
> review (both sessions are the same kind of model and share blind spots).
> (2) THE VALIDATOR DOES NOT FIX: a review is a dated file under
> docs/reviews/ with numbered findings, each with a severity and the
> evidence; the builder answers every finding (fixed in <commit>, or
> declined with the reason); the validator never edits the slice it reviews.
> (3) AFTER LANDING, not before: a review does not gate a landing; it
> follows it within the next working session.
> (4) THE CLOUD'S OWN RECORDS NEED A VALIDATOR TOO: the laptop (or Vitor by
> sampling) reviews the cloud's components and pairs; nobody reviews their
> own fits (C300).
> (5) A LIMIT, stated: the cloud cannot read the literature folder, so it
> checks a transcription only against an open-access primary or against a
> transcription committed to the tree.

> over the kept points:

> effect on a design enters through large margins or fractional exponents;
> (C) bubble TEMPERATURE (pairs): clean up to 1 K, warning 1-2 K, severe
> 2-4 K, refused above 4 K (unchanged).

> reason.  One home for the three tables is owed (today each tool carries

> **C300 (architect, 2026-11-11; step (c) of C298): the acceptance of a
> fitted pair is tightened BEFORE any more pairs are generated.**  Measured on
> main 2026-11-10 over the 132 public NRTL records: 84 `clean`, 19 `warning`,
> 17 `severe`, 12 ungraded (hand-curated).  Of the 84 clean, 62 rest on ONE
> stated temperature AND ONE laboratory with `heldOut none` (the P-x records of
> C291): their "clean" is the in-sample residual of the points they were
> fitted to, nothing that could have contradicted them.  Shipped cases outside
> curation that NAME a severe pair: solvent03 (benzene-nButanol), temperature02
> (ethyleneGlycol-water); a single-temperature clean pair: solvent03
> (cyclohexane-nButanol), solubility01 and cosmoSAC01 (nHexane-toluene) --
> name co-occurrence only, to be confirmed by a run.  RULES:
> 1. The grade is labelled for what it is: `fitGradeBasis inSample;` in every
>    graded record, and the engine's voice (src/thermo/FitGrade.H) says
>    "in-sample".  A held-out residual, when one exists, is recorded beside it,
>    never in place of it.
> 2. `clean` needs evidence able to contradict it: at least two stated
>    temperatures (isotherms, for P-x) AND at least two laboratories, OR a
>    held-out set that itself grades clean.  Otherwise the grade is CAPPED at
>    `warning` with the named reason (`fitGradeCap singleTemperature |
>    singleLaboratory`).  The 62 records are re-graded, not refitted: no
>    parameter moves.
> 3. `severe` records leave the default catalogue: the record and its evidence
>    stay in its curation case (data/curation/pairs/<a>-<b>/), the engine never
>    loads it by default, and a case that needs one carries it in its own
>    constant/ with the grade voiced.  The shipped cases that read one are
>    measured first; their numbers must not move.
> 4. Every tool that writes a record writes `review { by none; }` and stops
>    writing `humanReviewed`.  The engine reads a legacy `humanReviewed true`
>    as `by human` with no reviewer named, `false` as `by none` (C297's open
>    item).
> 5. Then C290's 466 pairs are graded by these rules and land; then C294 and
>    the 117 multi-isotherm pairs (C291).
> Validation: the re-grade moves no parameter; the voices change on the cases
> that read a re-graded record, measured by a run before and after.

> **C297 (Vitor, 2026-11-10, agreeing to C296 "excepto na questao da
> revisao": "ja ninguem tem tempo para andar a curar humanamente tudo!  Eu

> A RECORD SAYS WHO REVIEWED IT, AND WHAT WAS CHECKED.**  Adopted, with
> three conditions that make a model's review worth reading.  DECIDED:
>   1. `humanReviewed true|false` (a yes/no nobody will ever turn to yes at
>      this scale) is replaced by a `review {}` block: `by human|model|none;
>      reviewer "<name or model id>"; date; checked ( ... ); verdict
>      accepted|flagged|rejected; note "...";`.  `by none` is said in words
>      ("unreviewed"), never hidden.  The old key is still READ (backwards
>      compatibility): `humanReviewed true` = `by human`, false = `by none`.
>   2. A model review is a CHECKLIST, not an opinion, and `checked` names
>      the items it ran: the cited source opened and the points read
>      against it; units and composition basis; i/j direction; the dropped
>      points and the reason; the fit redrawn against a second laboratory
>      where one exists; no false liquid split inside the stated span; the
>      azeotrope (presence, T, x) against a measured one where one exists.
>   3. The reviewer is NOT the session that fitted the record (the fitter
>      grading itself is the in-sample problem again), and the model id and
>      date are written, because two models are two reviewers.
>   4. Review is not validation.  What a reviewer cannot change stays in
>      its own measured fields and is shown beside the review: held-out
>      points or none, number of laboratories, number of temperatures,
>      in-sample grade.  A single-temperature fit reviewed by anyone is
>      still a single-temperature fit.
>   5. The engine's announcement (Database.cpp:665, PairAudit.H:114) says
>      who reviewed, in the same line it now says "no human has reviewed".
>   6. A human sample keeps the model honest: a small random draw of
>      model-reviewed records read by a person, the disagreement rate
>      written in the review ledger.  Size and cadence not decided here.

> CORRECT THE DUTY, AND THE CORRECTION IS A NAMED TERM.**  Vitor's decision
> amends the 2026-06-27 heat-of-reaction contract (CLAUDE.md section 5): a
> reaction may declare a MEASURED heat of reaction (value, temperature, phase,
> source); the reactor's duty is then corrected by extent x (declared -
> computed from formation data at the same conditions), the stream
> enthalpies stay on the formation datum, and the correction is published
> beside the duty and as its own line in the energy report (never hidden in
> the duty).  The formation route stays the default; the mismatch is always
> printed.  An EduTool explains why a computed reaction heat on the
> ideal-gas route can be unreliable in the liquid phase and what the
> correction does.  The EduTool scope is put to Vitor before it is built.

> **C283 (Vitor, 2026-11-10, on the vapour-pressure fits that failed their
> held-out band: "isto nao e ciencia exata ... Por default um erro relativo de
> 5% chega e sobra! E um erro inferior a 1 grau K tambem!").  THE DEFAULT
> ACCEPTANCE OF A CURATION FIT.**  A fitted record is accepted by default when,
> on the held-out measurements, its MAXIMUM relative error is at most 5 % in
> every property judged relatively (pressure, composition, density, Cp,
> viscosity), and its maximum absolute error is below 1 K in temperature.  A
> case may declare another band (`acceptance {}`), with its reason; the
> default is announced when used.  The band derived from the held-out
> laboratory's own stated uncertainty is RETIRED as the acceptance test --
> laboratories disagree with each other by more than they claim, so it
> rejected curves far better than the estimates they would replace -- and is
> kept as information only.  Applies to `bin/choupo-curate vp` and `pair` and
> every fit-op acceptance default.  First applied in C281 step 3.
> **C283 amended (Vitor, same hour: "Eu usaria os dados dos laboratorios
> todos! Eventualmente descarto blatant outliers!").**  A curation fit uses
> EVERY laboratory's measurements, not one study to fit and another held out.
> Blatant outliers are discarded BY NAME and listed in the case (stated
> default: after the least-squares stage, a point whose relative error exceeds
> three times the 5 % band, i.e. 15 %, or 3 K in temperature; the fit is then
> repeated without it); acceptance (5 % max relative, < 1 K) is judged on all
> the points kept.  The one-study-fit / other-study-held-out partition of C16
> is RETIRED as the default for these pipelines.

> **C280 (Vitor, 2026-11-10, on the butanol-water fit: "Eu quando faco ajuste
> comeco por minimizar os residuos quadraticos pra ter uma estimativa inicial.
> Depois no final prefiro minimizar o erro maximo! Porque isso e que me da a
> garantia que nao apanho com um erro nas extremidades grande a estragar-me a
> previsao!" and "Excepto para a Temperatura, costumo focar-me no erro relativo
> medio e no maximo. Para T trabalho com valores absolutos").  `fitParameters`
> GETS A RELATIVE RESIDUAL AND A FINAL MINIMAX STAGE.**  Two parts: (1) a
> composition residual may be declared RELATIVE (a temperature residual stays
> absolute), and the report prints mean and maximum relative error for
> compositions, mean and maximum absolute error for T; (2) `objective`
> gains a second stage that starts from the least-squares answer and minimises
> the LARGEST error, announced as such, with both answers kept in the result.
> WHY IT IS NEEDED, measured on curate14 (landed with this entry): the
> five-parameter NRTL holds the butanol solubility in water flat (0.019 at 288
> K, 0.022 at 366 K, measured 0.016-0.021) where the two-parameter form took it
> to 0.067, and the held-out tie-line AAD is 0.0061; but in relative terms the
> water-rich liquid is 12 % mean / 24 % max in the fit set and SYSTEMATICALLY
> 15 % high above 320 K, because an absolute residual weighs a mole fraction of
> 0.02 twenty-five times less than one of 0.5.  The between-study scatter on
> that liquid is itself about 15 % (0.0159 to 0.0207 at 298.15 K).  THE PAIR IS
> NOT PROMOTED to `data/standards/parameters/NRTL/` until this stage has run on
> it.  Also ruled the same day and applied in curate14: a held-out bubble miss
> of 1.7 K was "para mim esta bem ... modelacao e por definicao sempre
> aproximada" -- the bubble band for a pair is the data's U95 PLUS the
> catalogue vapour-pressure error at the set's pressure (0.85 K here), never
> the U95 alone; and "a solubilidade tem de ficar bem" -- for a two-liquid
> pair the solubility against temperature is the first thing judged.  Still

> **C269 (Vitor, 2026-11-09, on the C266 pharmaceutical findings: "Avança.  Eu revejo depois.
> O que a teoria vê não precisa de ser martelado numericamente!"): THE WALK'S FINDINGS ARE
> FIXED NOW, AND THE ENGINEERING ITEMS ARE DECIDED BY THEORY, each decision written here for
> his review.**
> DISPLAY AND ENGINE ERRORS (no opinion in them): the sheet's number formatter (98 200 shown
> as 982); solids counted twice on stream cards; unit words the engine writes and the app
> refuses (`m3/yr`, `um`, `rpm`) -- one vocabulary, and a gate that parses every shipped
> design sheet with the app's parser; a sheet's molar F without the solids beside a mass
> flow with them; a Turton cost outside its correlation announced in the caveats, not the
> Log alone; the shift check per product; README links accepted by the app's parser (31
> READMEs still refused after C264's fix).
> DECIDED BY THEORY:
> (1) THE DRYER'S ISOTHERM.  A solid can dry no further than equilibrium with the air it is
> in contact with WHEN IT LEAVES.  A batch dried to its end point (a fluid-bed dryer of
> granules: evaporation falls to nothing, so the exhaust tends to the inlet air) ends in
> equilibrium with the INLET air; a continuous well-mixed or co-current dryer (a spray
> dryer) discharges its powder with the EXHAUST.  So the engine is right in both units
> (solidDryer reads the inlet, SolidDryer.cpp:170-172; sprayDryer the exhaust) and the three
> case texts that say "exhaust" for the fluid-bed dryer are wrong.  Fix the texts; the unit
> announces which air state its isotherm is read at, and the KPI's meaning is stated; no
> new key until a case needs the other contacting pattern.
> (2) TAX ON A LOSS.  A negative tax is a credit only if the owner has other taxable profit
> to set the loss against; a stand-alone project has none.  The current numbers stay (no
> golden moves on a default), the engine ANNOUNCES the assumption whenever a year's tax is
> negative, with its size, and a declared `economics` choice gives the stand-alone reading
> (no credit).  The pharmaceutical READMEs say which reading their NPV is.
> (3) sprayDryer06 (REA) equal to sprayDryer01 to the last digit: either the declared
> kinetics is not honoured (an engine defect, to be found first) or the case sits where the
> kinetics cannot bite; the case is moved to where it does, on its own declared data.
> (4) sprayDryer07, a 0.32 m chamber for a 0.1 m wheel: a rotary atomiser's chamber diameter

> **C263 (Vitor, 2026-11-09: "que tipo de compressor se usa para altas pressões?  Disseram-me
> que os de turbina necessitam de recirculação por causa do controlo ... era bom que a folha
> de especificação fosse mais concreta no tipo de compressor e que fizesse um bom design"):
> COMPRESSOR SELECTION AND DESIGN ON THE SPECIFICATION SHEET.**  Measured today: the unit
> (src/unitOperations/rotating/Compressor.H) is ONE isentropic stage specified by shaft power
> or P_out with a declared eta; CompressorSize.H sizes "a centrifugal compressor / blower" by
> power alone, no geometry; Turton prices it as centrifugal; nothing selects a type, counts
> stages or impellers, checks a discharge-temperature limit, or knows surge.  The reference
> plant builds its 150 bar make-up train by hand as two compressor units and an intercooler
> (MakeupComp1/2 discharge 420 / 425 K, N2Boost 474 K).  The engineering the sheet should
> carry: (1) TYPE by flow and pressure from a declared, sourced selection map -- dynamic
> (centrifugal, axial) for large flows, positive displacement (reciprocating, diaphragm for
> small high-purity flows, screw at moderate ratios) for small flows and the highest
> pressures; hydrogen's low molar mass makes the head per impeller small, so a centrifugal
> machine needs many impellers and reciprocating machines dominate small and medium H2 duties;
> (2) STAGES and INTERCOOLING from a declared discharge-temperature limit and per-stage ratio;
> (3) for a DYNAMIC machine the SURGE line and the ANTI-SURGE RECYCLE -- below the surge flow
> the machine cannot hold its head and the flow reverses, so a cooled spill-back from
> discharge to suction keeps the machine above it at low throughput: the sheet sizes the
> recycle valve and cooler for the declared surge margin and shows the turndown it buys;
> for a RECIPROCATING machine, capacity control by unloaders / clearance pockets / speed /
> spill-back, and no surge; (4) the data-sheet fields of the governing standards (API 617
> centrifugal, API 618 reciprocating), each limit read from a source, never recalled.
> Pedagogy too: an EduTool on compressor selection and surge (the head-flow curve, the surge
> line, what the recycle does to power).  ORDER: after the reference-plant slice lands (it
> edits the same compressors); scope to Vitor in two lines before dispatch.

> **C262 (Vitor, 2026-11-09: "em Dezembro vou ter de consolidar a forma como recebo feedback
> da comunidade.  Achas que se pode criar um depósito de casos de estudo auto-contidos que
> colaboradores queiram deixar?"): YES -- A COMMUNITY CASE REPOSITORY, A TIER APART FROM THE
> CURATED CORPUS; DESIGNED IN DECEMBER TOGETHER WITH THE FEEDBACK INTAKE (C261).**  Why it
> fits: a Choupo case is already a self-contained folder (the credo: every datum in
> constant/, verified by hiding data/standards), a sealed case already pins its catalogue,
> and the app already opens a case from a .zip -- which is also what a student's assistant
> produces (C257).  Shape proposed: (1) its OWN repository, not tutorials/: the curated corpus
> is golden-checked and gated, and a contributed case is a different level of trust -- the
> same split as data/standards vs data/local, and the same reason the public `proposed` tier
> was retired (a public middle tier is where third-party values leak in).  (2) Automatic
> admission, no human in the loop for the first rung: CI runs every submitted case on the
> released engine and refuses it unless it runs, is self-contained, closes every mass,
> element and energy balance it claims (rule 4b, the same gate), carries a header (what it
> is, sources) and passes check_source_licence (no NonCommercial or unlicensed values).
> (3) Three rungs, shown on the case: SUBMITTED (the CI passed), REVIEWED (a technical
> reviewer's record, C261), PROMOTED (copied into tutorials/ by the architect, with a golden
> -- the only rung that enters the corpus).  (4) Credit through the same registry as reviews
> (C261: a CONTRIBUTOR of a case, consent by the act of submitting under their own name), a
> licence the submitter states at submission (CC BY 4.0 for the case text and data that is
> theirs; DCO sign-off as the main project), and a gallery page on the site with
> "open in the app".  (5) Submission by a pull request or an issue form with the .zip
> attached.  Open questions for December: the licence of a case's prose vs the GPL of the

> **C260 (Vitor, 2026-11-09: a review of the `ip-strategy` EduTool by a friend, Karol Peirs,
> who examines at the European Patent Office, forwarded with "podes ver se dá para tu
> refletires?  E como fazemos para lhe dar crédito?  Temos de ver este ponto com
> cuidado"): THREE POINTS, ALL ACCEPTED, AND THE CREDIT HELD UNTIL HE CONSENTS TO ITS
> WORDING.**  (1) Section 2, "The costs are three." follows the Art. 64(3) sentence with no
> transition and reads as a non sequitur; it is a terse enumeration (disclosure, money,
> enforcement), not an invention, but a patent professional stumbled on it, so it is
> rewritten.  The C259 auditor of this page did not flag it -- a human expert reading
> as a reader catches what a line-by-line check passes.  (2) Section 8 says the EPC leaves
> infringement to national law (Art. 64(3)); true of the Convention, incomplete since the
> Unified Patent Court opened (2023-06-01): for the participating states, infringement of
> a Unitary Patent, and of a European patent not opted out, is decided by one court under
> the UPC Agreement.  For a page about patent strategy that is S2, not a footnote: a
> dedicated section on the UPC is added (jurisdiction, opt-out and the transitional
> period, divisions, what stays national -- prior use among it), every statement read in
> the UPC Agreement or on the court's / EPO's pages, never from memory.  (3) The worked
> case studies (section 19 on) are hard for a non-chemist: noted; each gets a two-line
> plain-language summary at its head, nothing cut.  CREDIT, decided: the existing CURATOR
> mechanism (AUTHORS `Curators`, registry.ts `curator`, check_curator_parity) is for a
> person who ANSWERS for the reviewed scope, with an affiliation drawn on the tool; an
> examiner of a patent office named with that office beside a patent-law page could be
> read as the office's endorsement, which is his employer's question, not ours.  So: until
> he says otherwise, an ACKNOWLEDGEMENT on the page, in a personal capacity, with no
> affiliation, saying what he read (the draft of <date>, sections 1-18, not the case
> studies) and that remaining errors are the project's; curator only if he reviews the
> revised page and wants it.  Nothing is written with his name until Vitor brings his
> written consent to the exact text and the spelling of his name (rule 00: consent of a
> named person stays Vitor's).  LANDED 2026-11-09 (eea569a68) with C259: the costs
> sentence, section 12 on the Unified Patent Court (UPCA read article by article in the OJ C 175
> PDF; Regulation 1257/2012; the EPO pages; Lisbon's local division from the court's own
> Presidium decision), the case studies' IN BRIEF summaries; not written because not
> verified: the central division's seats, the end of the transitional period.  The general
> corrected the brief: the prior-use RIGHT is national (UPCA Art. 28) but the UPC HEARS actions
> on it (Art. 32(1)(g)).  No name, no acknowledgement.  AMENDED the same day (Vitor): Karol is left aside until he
> approves; nothing carries his name, and Vitor is not asked to handle consent (C261).
> LANDING (Vitor, the same message thread: "na landing page devia de haver um link para
> afirmar isso?"): yes, but as ONE page "Who reviewed what" (every curator and

> **C259 (Vitor, 2026-11-09 morning: "Será que podes pôr o general em modo Fable a rever
> os EduTools todos com muito cuidado, para em Dezembro eu não ficar embaraçado perante os
> meus colegas?"): A SCIENTIFIC AUDIT OF EVERY EDUTOOL LESSON, READ-ONLY FIRST.**  This is

> reaction enthalpy to the steam raised AND to the adiabatic rise "in the same
> proportion"; standardStateLesson.ts:313 says not to carry that percentage to either
> without closing those balances.  Two pages, two conclusions; the second is the true
> one in general (the first holds only for an isothermal balance with feed and
> products at the reactor temperature, which the page does not say).
> (C) epsilonNtuLesson.ts:81 "across a phase change the log-mean of the terminal
> temperatures is not the driving force at all" -- false as a general statement: an
> isothermal condenser against a single-phase coolant is the textbook case where the
> LMTD is exact (C_r = 0); it fails with desuperheating, subcooling or a gliding
> temperature.  "What this unit models" was written as "what the method allows".
> (D) approachToEquilibriumLesson.ts:469 "read the composition from the shifted run
> and everything else from the unshifted one": the unshifted run's duty belongs to
> the UNSHIFTED composition; the duty of a declared approach is H_out(T physical,
> shifted composition) - H_in.  To be checked against what EquilibriumReactor.cpp
> does before the sentence "which is what the engine itself does" is kept.
> (E) levenspielLesson.ts:171 a stirred tank provides the seed of an autocatalytic
> reaction "by construction": with no product in the feed or the charge, r = k C_A C_P
> gives dC_P/dt = 0 at C_P = 0 -- back-mixing SUSTAINS a seed, it does not create
> one; the washout state is always a solution.  Existence of a steady state against
> the possibility of start-up: a better lesson than the sentence it replaces.
> (F) dataReconciliationLesson.ts:290 "the multiplier is fixed by the balance's own
> residual: a balance that closed at the readings would get zero", beside its own
> lambda = (A C A^T)^-1 r: balances sharing a meter are coupled, so r_k = 0 does not
> give lambda_k = 0.
> (G) batchMembraneLesson.ts:786-793 "a crossflow module CAN correlate [the film
> coefficient] ... and a stirred vessel cannot" -- stirred cells have mass-transfer
> correlations; what is missing is a declared geometry in THIS unit; likewise
> "exactly two pure batch operations" (:147) and "in real equipment the flux falls"
> (:417) state the tool's scope and one mechanism as universals.  In Vitor's own field.
> WHY THEY STOOD.  Every lesson claim ABOUT THE ENGINE is held to a file:line and
> re-checked by a gate (check_lesson_symbols, the anchors tests); nothing holds a
> sentence about PHYSICS.  The 2026-08-31 audit (43 defects) read the lessons against
> the engine they cite, the same lens.  A sentence can be perfectly cited and
> scientifically false -- (A) is cited to the case and misreads its own number.
> ON THE PEDAGOGY the review agrees with what Vitor said the same night and what was
> already decided (C251 revised: no sequence is offered until one is written with
> him); its proposed orders (tear topology before relaxation; binary equilibrium
> before the flash; stages -> efficiency and hydraulics -> dimensions before cost)
> are taken as input for that writing.  Its point on MIXED LEVELS is right and is the
> C246 finding generalised: physics, the experiment, the implementation and the
> development history are interleaved in one paragraph (dates of corrections, "the
> owner's doubt", C++ lines in mid-argument).
> DECISIONS: (1) the seven are fixed NOW, each with a test that recomputes the
> corrected statement (A from the golden; F and E by a numeric counterexample; C by
