> **C253 (the architect, 2026-11-09 night.  Vitor asked, out of curiosity and not as an
> order -- "eu só estava a perguntar por curiosidade" -- whether the practice followed is
> that of a responsible engineer on a project of this size, and left the answer to the
> architect's judgement: "faz o que achares que ajuda mais este desenvolvimento do
> Choupo"): THE ENGINEERING PRACTICE GAP, NAMED AND RANKED; THE DECISION IS THE
> ARCHITECT'S.**  Why it helps the development and is not ceremony: a sweep on a server
> gives Vitor his laptop back for half an hour at a time, and a sanitizer build finds
> the class of C++ fault no golden can see; both are cheap.  What stands: regression over the whole corpus with
> per-case references, 320 contract gates, validation sized by reach with the full sweep
> on a written reason, decision records, isolated branches, one serial integration lane,
> generated files regenerated.  What is below a serious project's bar: (1) no continuous
> integration on a server -- every sweep runs on Vitor's laptop and competes with his own
> work; (2) no diff review -- the commander reads the generals' REPORTS, and the night's
> gate-bypass attempt (C249 c) was caught by an automatic warning, not by a reader of the
> diff; (3) one actor with direct push to main, no branch protection (delegated, and a
> risk nonetheless); (4) large batches (seven branches in two lots tonight) that make a
> failure harder to attribute; (5) no sanitizer build, no coverage; (6) the generals
> need too much supervision (one exhausted itself before a test, one bypassed a gate,
> two ran the wrong binary).  DECISION, by cost: (a) CI on GitHub Actions: `--fast` and
> the gates that need no case on every push to main and on every branch, the full
> sweep nightly, on GitHub's runner (the WASM/guide steps stay local; `check_build_fresh`
> and the timing CSV must tolerate the runner) -- the existing workflow builds and
> verifies only (RELEASING.md), so this extends it, never a second Pages deploy;
> (b) the commander reads the DIFF of every general's commit that touches a test, a
> gate or a schema, and a sample of the rest, before integrating -- a rule, not a tool,
> added to the fleet doctrine; (c) a weekly `-fsanitize=address,undefined` build of
> `--fast` as a gate-selftest sibling; (d) smaller batches except under a deadline
> (tonight's reason: the 11-09 tutorial).  (a) and (c) are one general after batch-2 AND after C252 (the student-facing
> work comes first); (b) and (d) start now.

> **C247 (Vitor, 2026-11-08: "sabes que há um EduTool sobre projeto de chaminés? ... equações
> gaussianas com coeficientes de dispersão e tabelas famosas em função das condições

> hour: there is NONE -- 76 tools in the registry, the safety ladder exists
> (process-safety, overpressure, pool-fire, bund, plant-layout, gmp-layout) and nothing
> touches atmospheric dispersion; "plume" appears only in the cooling-tower and pool-fire
> prose.  So the question is read as a proposal, and it is accepted: the stack is the
> one sized item of a fired unit that the layout page cannot place without it, and the
> method is public-domain and self-contained.  DECISION: tool `stack-dispersion`, next
> rung of the safety/environment ladder after `pool-fire`, theory chapter in the
> theoryGuide.  THE SPINE: (1) the Gaussian plume for a continuous point source,
> C(x,y,z) = Q/(2 pi u sigma_y sigma_z) exp(-y^2/2sigma_y^2) [exp(-(z-H)^2/2sigma_z^2) +
> exp(-(z+H)^2/2sigma_z^2)], the reflection term derived, not asserted; (2) the
> Pasquill-Gifford stability classes A-F read from a day/night, insolation and wind-speed
> table (Pasquill 1961; Turner 1970 Workbook, US EPA, public domain) -- the "famous
> table" he names, shown as the table and as a picker; (3) sigma_y(x), sigma_z(x) by
> class, Briggs' rural and urban fits (Briggs 1973, Gifford 1976), drawn, with the
> ORIGIN of each coefficient stated and the 100 m - 10 km window declared; (4) plume
> rise: Briggs' buoyancy-flux formulae (F = g v_s d^2 (T_s - T_a)/(4 T_s), the two
> regimes and the final rise), effective height H = h_s + delta h, momentum rise for a
> cold jet; (5) the ground-level maximum and WHERE it falls, derived from dC/dx = 0 for
> the class, and the DESIGN question inverted: the least stack height for which the
> maximum GLC stays under a declared limit value, across the worst class of the
> table; (6) the downwash rule (good-engineering-practice height = H_b + 1.5 L) as the
> other constraint.  FOUR LIVE FIGURES: the class picker (day/night, sun, wind) that
> recolours everything; the plume side view with the sigma envelopes and the reflected
> image source; GLC along the axis with the maximum marked, a stack-height slider and
> the limit line; the isopleth on a plan view with the fence, reusing the layout page's
> drawing.  ENGINE HALF: a real fired unit's flue gas from a run (flow, T, composition
> -> Q of SO2/NOx/CO2 and the buoyancy flux), read from the result and never
> recomputed, so the exercise starts from Choupo's own plant; the dispersion itself is

> named up front: no terrain, no building wake beyond the GEP rule, no chemistry in the
> plume, no averaging-time correction unless cited.  Sources: Turner 1970 (EPA AP-26),

> **C246 (Vitor, 2026-11-08: "ao contrário do OpenFOAM, não deixa o utilizador especificar
> os coeficientes de sub-relaxação ... podia haver valores default e depois o user podia
> fazer tinkering ... ou a sub-relaxação não é a metodologia mais adequada"): THE SOLVER
> KNOBS A CASE MAY TURN.**  MEASURED the same hour: `system/solverDict` already carries
> the recycle plan (`recycleSolver Newton|Wegstein`, `recycleTol`, `recycleMaxIter`,
> `recycleWegsteinQmin/Qmax` -- Wegstein's q IS a relaxation factor in disguise: the
> update is q x + (1 - q) G(x), so w = 1 - q; q = 0 is direct substitution, q = 0.5 the
> 50/50 average, q < 0 acceleration (CORRECTED by the C246 general, 11-08 night: this
> entry, Wegstein.H and a wegsteinMath.ts comment had "q = -1 is the 50/50 average",
> which is w = 2, a doubled step; and the engine's default clamp [-1, 0] keeps w in
> [1, 2], so Choupo's Wegstein NEVER under-relaxes -- on an oscillating loop the clamp
> makes it plain direct substitution, which is why the relaxation rung is worth
> having) -- and the
> dominant-eigenvalue options, every defaulted one announced; Flowsheet.cpp recScalar)
> and per-unit-TYPE blocks reached through `buildAugmentedDict` (Flowsheet.cpp:1066,
> 1126; `isothermalFlash { tolerance maxIter maxOuterIter outerAccelerator
> compositionTol }` is read at IsothermalFlash.cpp:1940-1948).  What a case CANNOT set:
> the Newton globalisation of a unit -- NDOptions maxStep (the per-unknown step cap,
> which is Newton's honest analogue of a relaxation factor: "T moves at most 10 K per
> iteration"), the T box, the line search, maxStalledSteps -- all fixed by each caller
> since C245 slice 1-2; and no plain `relaxation` word exists anywhere, so a student who
> knows OpenFOAM's `relaxationFactors` finds nothing.  Only `recycleWegsteinQmin` is
> documented (docs/ai/patterns.md:327).  JUDGEMENT on the methodology: a FIXED
> under-relaxation factor is the right tool for a segregated fixed-point scheme (SIMPLE,
> and the tear loop of a sequential-modular simulator), and the wrong default for Newton,
> where the line search damps only the iterates that need it and a fixed factor slows
> every one; the step CAP, however, is legitimate in Newton and is what a user tinkers
> with.  DECISION (architect, rule 00): (1) document the grammar that exists, in
> docs/ai/dict-syntax.md and the user guide, with Wegstein's q read as relaxation (w = 1 - q);
> (2) add `recycleRelaxation` (0 < w <= 1) for the direct-substitution tear loop and
> make `recycleSolver directSubstitution` a named choice, so the three rungs read
> relaxation -> Wegstein -> Newton; (3) per-unit-type Newton knobs in solverDict mapped
> onto NDOptions -- `distillationColumn { maxStepT 10 K; maxStepX 0.1; lineSearch
> armijo|none; maxIter; tolerance; }`, likewise `cstr`, `gibbsReactor`, the tear Newton
> (`recycleMaxStep`) -- defaults as today, every override ANNOUNCED with its value (no
> silent crutch: the aid is visible and the student's), a value outside its range refused
> by name; (4) the GUI's run log shows the announced knobs beside the convergence plot.
> BUILT (11-08/09 night, one general, five commits, scope 39/0 on every tear case,
> --fast 77/0, no golden moved): E1 the grammar documented (dict-syntax.md, userGuide);
> E2 `recycleSolver directSubstitution;` and `recycleRelaxation w;` (0 < w <= 1,

> (5) AN EDUTOOL ON RELAXATION (Vitor, the same evening: "devia de haver um EduTool sobre a
> questão da sub-relaxação onde tu explicas tudo o que disseste").  MEASURED: the Wegstein
> lesson (gui/src/ui/methods/wegsteinLesson.ts, eight steps, a declared linear toy plus
> the real engine on a recycle) and the tear-streams lesson exist; neither says the word

> not.  DECISION: a new tool `relaxation`, sibling of `wegstein` in the registry, theory
> chapter in the theoryGuide (manuals are part of the unit).  THE SPINE: a recycle is a
> fixed-point problem x = g(x); direct substitution converges when |g'| < 1 and crawls
> or diverges otherwise; relaxation x+ = (1-w) x + w g(x) changes the slope to
> 1 - w + w g', so a w < 1 tames a g' < -1 (the oscillating loop) and NO w rescues a
> g' > 1 (the runaway loop) -- a slider on the lesson's toy shows both, with the
> optimal w = 1/(1-g') for the linear case derived; Wegstein is that same formula with
> w = 1 - q chosen per variable from the last two iterates (so its q is an adaptive
> relaxation, the lesson states the identity and links to the Wegstein tool); Newton is
> the limit where the whole slope is used, and its line search is the adaptive factor
> on the merit function, which is why a FIXED factor is the wrong default for Newton
> and a per-variable step CAP is the honest knob; last, the segregated CFD solvers the
> students meet elsewhere (SIMPLE-type pressure-velocity coupling, OpenFOAM's
> `relaxationFactors`) need a fixed factor because their inner problem is linearised
> and segregated, and a sequential-modular flowsheet's tear loop is the same kind of
> problem while a unit's Newton is not.  THE ENGINE HALF of the tool runs a real recycle
> under `recycleSolver directSubstitution; recycleRelaxation w;` for three values of w
> and plots the tear residual per pass, so it lands WITH item (2), never before (a page
> must not teach a knob the engine lacks).  Every engine claim cited by file:line, every
> symbol glossed, tests recompute the toy against the tool's own math.

> **C235, DESIGN OF THE LIQUID RUNG (architect, 2026-11-07).**  `speciesPhaseEnthalpy`
> retired the Watson-slope liquid because it overrode a DECLARED Cp (the mheatx
> +10 %), and that stands: INSIDE the liquid Cp's declared `Trange` the rung is
> Kirchhoff.  The defect is only ABOVE it, where the rung integrates a correlation
> past its data while the record holds a better statement of the same slope: the
> ChemSep windows end at Tb, so above Tmax the latent-heat correlation is the only
> thing the record says about the liquid.  RULE: for T > Tmax, h_L(T) = h_L(Tmax) +
> [h_ig(T) - Hvap_W(T)] - [h_ig(Tmax) - Hvap_W(Tmax)], continuous in h, with a kink
> in Cp, announced once per component.  The offset at Tmax is kept, never forced to
> zero (a jump in h would be heat from nowhere).  Computed on column19's fixed
> profile: Q_reb 7883.7 kW (+3.2 % on the source case); offsets -667..+115 J/mol, and
> +1527 for methanol, whose +1.5 kJ/mol is a finding about its own record.  Reaches
> every case with a liquid above its window, so the sweep and the moved-row list go
> with it.  (B) the feed's state resolved and priced at the STREAM's pressure lands
> in the same slice.  (A) phi_sat with H_res,sat in the liquid leg stays a separate
> slice, after column19 reads right under the ideal vapour.

> **C235, CORRECTION (architect, 2026-11-07, same day; the entry below reads
> the 8 % wrongly): THE DUTIES ARE A LIQUID Cp EXTRAPOLATED, NOT THE IDEAL VAPOUR.**
> The liquid rung is Kirchhoff from 298 K on `liquidHeatCapacity` where the record
> has one, not h_ig - Hvap(T).  MTBE's correlation ends at 328.35 K and the reboiler
> is at 401 K (the C4s end at 261-277 K, methanol at 340 K): the extrapolation is
> announced and legitimate (I4), and it makes the latent the column prices at 401 K
> 24.14 kJ/mol against the record's own Watson 22.84.  Recomputed by hand from the
> published stage 14-15 profile, this rung gives Q_reb 8282.4 kW, the engine's own
> number to 0.1 kW, and the Watson rung 7846.3.  Measured on the whole column, in a
> scratch copy of the catalogue with the nine `liquidHeatCapacity` blocks removed
> (the first attempt moved nothing: a case record is overlaid field by field on the
> standards, so deleting it from the case alone restores the catalogue's): Q_cond
> 7.66 MW (+3.5 %), Q_reb 7.85 MW (+2.7 %), T_top 50.9 C, T_bottom 128.1 C, conversion
> 99.21 %, ideal vapour.  The source case reads 7.40 / 7.64 MW.  So the "+2.5 % under
> SRK" below is NOT evidence about the vapour: the liquid rung ignores the EoS, so an
> EoS vapour publishes a latent of Hvap + H_res, lower than the record's, and that
> reading came partly from this double count.  The remaining +3 % is not explained
> yet.  NOT DONE: no engine change.  Removing liquid Cp is the measurement, never the

> **C235 (architect, 2026-11-07, chasing the 8 % duties of the MTBE witness):
> TWO ENGINE DEFECTS THE IDEAL VAPOUR HID.**  column19 under `idealGas` closes its
> first law at 0.0 kW and reads Q_cond 8.02 / Q_reb 8.28 MW against the source
> case's 7.40 / 7.64 (+8.4 % on both), Q_reb - Q_cond = +0.26 against +0.24 MW.
> The boil-up is fixed at 1200 kmol/h in both, so the gap is a latent heat, 24.84
> against 22.92 kJ/mol.  The same case with `fugacityModel SRK` (a copy, unsealed,
> nothing committed): Q_reb 7.83 MW (+2.5 %, the drop of 5.5 % is the 1.34 kJ/mol
> a Redlich-Kwong vapour at 7 bar predicts by hand), BUT T_top 45.0 C, T_bottom
> 120.9 C (-6 and -7 K) and Q_cond 10.54 MW, and the plant's FIRST LAW OPENS:
> residual -2693 kW (14.7 %).  (A) THE PURE-LIQUID FUGACITY HAS NO phi_sat:
> `LiquidPhase::fEffective` is gamma x Psat, so with an EoS vapour K = gamma Psat /
> (phi_V P) counts the vapour non-ideality on one side only; at 401 K ln phi_V is
> about -0.14, and d ln P/dT = dHvap/(R T^2) = 0.0186 /K gives -7.5 K, the shift
> measured.  gamma-phi with an EoS vapour needs phi_i^sat(T) (and Poynting,
> declared) in the reference fugacity.  (B) A FEED ABOVE THE COLUMN'S PRESSURE IS
> PRICED AT THE COLUMN'S PRESSURE: `feedEnthalpy(*r.state, r.F, r.T, P, ...)`
> resolves and prices the feed at (T_feed, P_column), while the stream and the
> energy report carry it at its own P.  The C4 feed is a liquid at 323.15 K, 10
> bar; at 7 bar it resolves past its bubble point (q = -0.02), so the column books
> about 17 kJ/mol the stream never carried: the whole -2693 kW.  Under the ideal
> vapour it stays subcooled at 7 bar and hides.  This is CLAUDE.md's family "the
> state a unit computes with is not the state its streams carry".  The fix is
> the conservation law: a feed enters with the enthalpy its stream carries, and
> the letdown is an adiabatic flash at the stage.  A THIRD QUESTION for the same
> slice: the liquid rung is the ideal gas minus the latent heat, so an EoS vapour
> makes the published latent h_V(real) - h_L, not the rung's own number: to be
> measured, not assumed.

> **C209. A SECTOR THAT SAYS HOW MANY TIMES IT IS REPEATED (Vitor, 2026-11-02
> night, about swro01_campoDalias: "no flowsheet devia haver forma de
> notificar isso ... qualquer envolucro que dissesse quantas vezes se tem de
> multiplicar"; his premise: in modern chemical industry a unit passes its
> economic maximum size and the engineer designs ONE train, repeated in
> parallel).**  MEASURED today: the case carries the SUM of six identical
> trains (`vessels 1398` = 6 x 233; pumps and exchanger at six times a train's
> flow) and declares `trains { count 6; }` separately in the postDict for the
> per-train sizing (`TrainSplit.H` in the sizing sources) -- the number six has TWO homes.
> DECIDED, the architect's design: a sector declares `repeat N;` and holds ONE
> train at a train's flows; the streams that cross its boundary carry the PLANT
> TOTAL and the engine splits inlets by N and sums outlets (no hand arithmetic);
> what is shared (intake, pretreatment, product tank, CIP, building) lives
> outside the wrapper; the stream table shows "per train" and "x N = total",
> the three balances count the total; the per-train sizing reads `repeat` and
> the postDict `trains { count }` goes (one home for N); the GUI draws the
> sector as a stacked box labelled "x N" (the PFD convention for parallel
> units).  A recycle that crosses the wrapper from one train to another REFUSES
> by name.  Phase 2, not now: non-identical trains (one stopped, a spare,
> N+1), uneven distribution over the header -- they belong with the digital
> twin (C203), where stopping a train is an operating scenario.  CHECKED
> ONLINE (2026-11-02, Vitor asked whether this is good flowsheet practice):
> the PFD convention of Turton et al. (course slides read, KFUPM CHE 425
> chapter 1, slides 9-10) is "XX-YZZ A/B ... A/B identifies parallel units or
> backup units not shown on a PFD" -- equipment in the same service is drawn
> ONCE and its parallel or spare copies are carried by the tag suffix, which
> matches drawing one train; so the repeated sector's item tags carry the
> train letter (A..F) beside the "x N" box, in the convention's own form.
> Seawater RO plants are built as many identical, independently operable
> trains with redundancy by count (Perth 12 SWRO trains; a DOE workshop slide
> lists the number and size of trains and the redundant capacity among the
> core design choices) -- the C209 premise holds for this case.  NOT found:
> any public source stating how simulators should model identical trains, so
> "one train with a multiplicity" is Choupo's design choice, argued above, and
> is not to be described as an industry standard.  Migration:
> swro01_campoDalias is the witness (its goldens move only by the
> representation, which the list in the commit shows).  Placed first in Beyond
> a week.

> **C204. AN EDUTOOL ON WHERE TO PLACE THE CONTROL LOOPS IN THE COMMON UNIT
> OPERATIONS, WITH A PARETO ANALYSIS (Vitor, 2026-11-02: "Achas bem um
> EduTools sobre estrategias de colocacao do sistema de controlo nas
> operacoes unitarias mais comuns? Faz uma analise pareto.").**  RECORDED;
> the Pareto analysis was brought to Vitor in the session the same day, with
> the proposed pedagogical scope and the order of unit dynamics it implies for
> C203; NOTHING dispatched before his answer on the scope (CLAUDE.md §10: a
> pedagogical scope is put to Vitor first).  Measured facts it rests on:
> corpus unit frequencies (steady + plant + batch/plant flowsheets:
> isothermalFlash 97, mixer 49, splitter 42, spiralWoundModule 42,
> phaseChanger 37, gibbsReactor 36, distillationColumn 34, heater 26,
> evaporator 24, cstr 22, compressor 21, pump 13, heatExchanger 13, pfr 12);
> the only time-integrated units are `dynamicCSTR` (CONSTANT volume,
> DynamicCSTR.H:33 -- so no level loop can be shown today), the
> `quasiSteady` adapter and `williamsOttoPlant`; controllers are PID,
> Schedule and Signal, acting on unit parameters (ctrl01: cv T, mv T_jacket).
> **THE PARETO, as brought to Vitor (the content a general builds from; the
> order is engineering judgement after Luyben, Tyreus & Luyben, Plantwide
> Process Control (1998) and Skogestad, Comput. Chem. Eng. 28 (2004) 219 --
> NOT read in the session, so no number is quoted from them).**  Each page:
> the rule, the exception taught WITH it, a case that runs.
> (1) LIQUID INVENTORY: level by the OUTFLOW downstream of the throughput
> manipulator; exceptions: upstream of it, level by the INFLOW; a surge tank
> takes averaging (P-only) control, not a tight PI; a reflux drum is
> controlled by the LARGEST stream (reflux, not distillate, when R >> 1).
> (2) GAS INVENTORY (pressure): by the vapour outflow or the heat removal;
> exceptions: column pressure by the condenser duty; a compressor by speed,
> its anti-surge a separate loop.  (3) FLOW AND RATIO: one flow sets the
> throughput, the others follow by ratio; exceptions: one valve per line; a
> positive-displacement pump by speed or recycle, never a valve on its
> discharge.  (4) TEMPERATURE BY A UTILITY: the utility flow or a bypass;
> exceptions: an exothermic reactor open-loop unstable needs a jacket
> cascade; a process-process exchanger is controlled by the bypass, not the
> flow.  (5) COMPOSITION / QUALITY: inferred from a tray temperature;
> exceptions: one composition is easy, two couple (RGA); the temperature is
> pressure-compensated.  (6) CONSTRAINTS AND SAFETY (override, split range,
> anti-surge) are taught last, as exceptions to the five.  Loops 1-4 are
> most of a plant's loops; 5 carries the most value per loop.  Plus one
> METHOD page: count the control degrees of freedom, choose the throughput
> manipulator, close the inventories in the right direction, then quality.
> Order of unit dynamics this implies (C205): tank with level, flash drum,
> exchanger, variable-volume CSTR, RO train, the column's inventories.

> **C200. ANY LLM MUST LEARN CHOUPO FROM A BRIEF IT ACTUALLY READS, AND DESIGN
> BEFORE IT COPIES (Vitor, 2026-11-02, URGENT: "os alunos podem interagir com o
> choupo.org atraves de ti usando qualquer LLM ... pedem a LLM um projeto, ou
> uma consulta e ajuste de propriedades termofisicas; a LLM aprende Choupo e
> prepara um .zip; o aluno abre-o na GUI e faz a curadoria e a validacao ...
> mas a LLM salta diretamente para um tutorial semelhante e nao faz um
> trabalho otimizado ... revê toda a documentacao que qualquer LLM vai ler,
> numa linguagem que minimize os tokens e maximize a aprendizagem").**
> MEASURED 2026-11-02: docs/ai/ is 887 126 bytes (about 220 000 tokens), 20
> files; the largest are unit-ops.md 193 KB, schemas-reference.md 157 KB,
> case-layout.md 112 KB, components.md 75 KB, gui-credo.md 70 KB (a GUI-design
> file, irrelevant to a student's LLM), pitfalls.md 41 KB; AGENTS.md is 5 KB and
> is the only entry a chat reads first; `bin/llmctx` concatenates the lot.  No
> chat window holds that with attention, so an LLM reads the head, matches a
> tutorial by name and copies it: the symptom is the size, not the model.
> ARCHITECTURE (the architect's, to be tested, not assumed): (1) a KERNEL BRIEF
> of about 6-8 k tokens every LLM reads first: what Choupo is, the glass-box
> rules, the case layout, the WORKFLOW with its mandatory first step -- write a
> DESIGN BRIEF (basis, units, thermo package and why, what is validated against
> what, what is NOT modelled) BEFORE opening any tutorial; tutorials are syntax
> examples only AFTER the design -- the twelve traps that cost a student a
> wrong answer at exit 0, the zip contract (what the GUI opens), how to check
> (bin/choupo-lint, and what to tell the student to click); (2) TASK PACKS of 3-6 k
> tokens each, loaded on demand from an INDEX one screen long: property
> consultation and fit, a membrane design, a distillation, a reactor, a
> crystalliser, a pharmaceutical plant, ...; (3) a GENERATED reference -- one line per unit
> and per key with its unit, produced from the engine's own contracts
> (`choupoSolve --describe-units`, the schemas), never hand-copied; (4) every
> pack in a terse, telegraphic form (keys and tables, no narrative), with the
> history and the argument moved to the design records a person reads.  The
> reference tools exist for the student: choupo-lint validates a case without
> solving it.  EVALUATION, because a brief is judged by what an LLM does with
> it, not by its look: a fixed set of 8-10 representative student tasks, each
> given to a proxy LLM holding ONLY the packs (Haiku and Sonnet are the proxy:
> if a small model succeeds a large one will), scored mechanically -- the zip
> passes choupo-lint, solves, its balances close, it states a design basis,
> it does NOT copy a tutorial wholesale (a similarity measure against the
> corpus), and its token cost is recorded.  PHASES: A the evaluation harness and
> the baseline (today's llmctx: the number to beat), B the kernel brief and
> the index, C the packs, D the generated reference, E the second measurement
> and the delta.  MODEL: the architecture, the protocol and the eval design are
> the Opus-class work (one session); the packs, the generators and the
> harness are Sonnet generals'.

> **C198 ROUTE FOR SEAWATER (the architect, 2026-11-02, after the measurement
> study `docs/design/boron-in-seawater-apparent-pka-study.md`, Vitor having
> asked whether Stage 1 is good practice):**  Stage 1 stays as LANDED -- the
> mechanism (two forms, a pH split, an exact effective rejection) and the
> lesson, calibrated at the data sheet's pH, where the pKa error largely
> cancels; it is NOT a quantitative tool for extrapolating in pH, and its
> case says so.  Measured: boron's apparent pK in reference seawater (Millero
> 2008 via TEOS-10 Table D.3; Dickson 1990 moved to the engine's scale, 8.82)
> is 9.12 under Davies with or without the major-ion pairs, 8.95 with the
> Ca/Mg borate complexes, and 8.84 under `pitzerHMW` with the tree's own
> boron binaries plus the two `pitzer.dat` complexes (+0.016); the residual
> +0.13 under Davies is a sodium-borate interaction no public ion-association
> database carries, and fitting one to Dickson would make the check the fit.
> DECIDED: **seawater boron is a Pitzer (`pitzerHMW`) route; Davies stays for
> the low-salinity second pass and brackish feeds.**  Caveat recorded, not
> hidden: the Pitzer boron parameters were themselves fitted to seawater
> measurements of the kind Dickson's constant rests on, so the agreement
> confirms the transcription and the engine, not an independent prediction.
> NEXT (curation, before any case uses it): the BOH4 / CaBOH4 / MgBOH4
> formation records and the eight Pitzer mixing records the study lists, each
> from its PRIMARY -- Felmy & Weare, Geochim. Cosmochim. Acta 50 (1986) 2771
> must be READ first (not read in the session; Vitor's library access may be
> the route); the borate constant of the Pitzer route is the one of THAT
> parameterisation (-9.239), never mixed with phreeqc.dat's -9.24 + dH, which
> stays the Davies route's (D2: identity per curated parameterisation).  Then
> Stage 2 (pH along the channel) on the seawater feed as major ions.

> **C198. BORON IN REVERSE OSMOSIS AS TWO SPECIES SPLIT BY THE pH (Vitor,
> 2026-11-01: "o boro e para modelar"; C194 shipped it as a declared lumped
> approximation; 2026-11-02, Opus switched on by Vitor: "faz a proposta do
> boro").**  PROPOSAL written, no code:
> docs/design/boron-in-reverse-osmosis-proposal.md.  It measures the engine first
> (the module reads pH only in `scaling {}`, SpiralWoundModule.cpp:1053-1066;
> SDEM already carries neutral and charged species, SDEM.cpp:302-318; a
> stream's pH is report-only, ProcessStream.H:185-245; the carbonate network
> and water dissociation are curated, no boric-acid record exists) and
> recommends: STAGE 1 now -- a curated `BOH4-formation` record from a primary
> source, the module splits boron by alpha = 1/(1+10^(pKa-pH)) at a DECLARED
> inlet pH and transports each form with its own permeance, the two
> permeances inverted from the data sheet's TWO pH-labelled rated tests (91 %
> at pH 8, 95 % at pH 10: identifiable because alpha differs), recombined into
> the apparent boron component, the frozen split ANNOUNCED, a held-out measured
> point if an open primary source can be read; STAGE 2 after its own ADR -- the
> pH COMPUTED from the carbonate system carried as real solutes, resolved at a
> unit's inlet (one home), CO2 passing the membrane, a caustic dosing mixer
> under a `designSpec` on pH and the caustic as a reagent cost; STAGE 3 (the
> twelve ions under SDEM) not recommended -- no per-ion permeances exist for
> these membranes.  pKa: a thermodynamic constant plus the declared activity
> model as the engine route, Dickson's conditional seawater constant as the
> validation anchor, never mixed.  TWO QUESTIONS PUT TO VITOR (his research
> area): the pKa route in seawater; whether the split frozen at the inlet pH is
> acceptable for the teaching case until Stage 2.
> DECIDED 2026-11-02 (Vitor: "usa a constante termodinamica e congela o pH a
> entrada"): (1) the engine's route is the THERMODYNAMIC constant with its
> enthalpy plus the case's declared activity model (Dickson's conditional
> seawater constant is the validation anchor only, never mixed in); (2) the
> split is FROZEN at the module inlet's pH, announced on every run, until Stage
> 2 resolves pH per station.  Stage 1 dispatched to a general the same hour.
> STATUS: DECIDED 2026-11-02; Stage 1 with a general.

> **C199. A DESALINATION PLANT IS TRAINS AND RACKS, NOT ONE GIANT PUMP AND
> ONE VESSEL BANK (Vitor, 2026-11-02, after seeing swro01_campoDalias's layout:
> "numa instalacao real ha limite para a dimensao maxima das bombas e dos
> recuperadores de pressao e a industria organiza aquilo por clusters de
> bombeagem e recuperacao de pressao! E era importante fazer o layout 3D dos
> racks de vasos de pressao dentro do pavilhao e plantas 2D. Ve online as boas
> praticas").**  PRACTICES READ ONLINE 2026-11-02 (open pages; vendor and trade
> sources, no standard; NO numeric clearance or spacing was found in any open
> source, so those stay author-set and are said so): (1) a large SWRO plant is
> a set of TRAINS, one HP pump and one pressure-exchanger array per train, or a
> `pressure centre` (a few large HP pumps and boosters feeding many racks
> through a common header): Danfoss, `multiple trains for large SWRO plants`
> (a SEARCH SUMMARY of that page, which a reader could not open -- 403 --: 24
> trains of 1041 m3/h against 8 pressure-centre trains of 3125 m3/h, efficiency
> above 87 % against above 90 %; NOT verified and NOT used by the guide); Sulzer's MSD-RO
> pump covers SWRO trains of 20 000-30 000 m3/d; Ebara supplied Carlsbad with 4
> axially split multistage pumps, 3 running and 1 spare; (2) a pressure
> exchanger is a MODULAR device: Energy Recovery's PX Q650 takes 250-650 gpm
> per device, up to 83 bar, mixing as low as 2 %, so a train carries an ARRAY
> sized by ceil(flow / device flow), and the vendor sizes pre-engineered arrays
> per train capacity (the 250-650 gpm window of the Q650 is from a search
> summary of the press release; the series page read gives 20-650 gpm); (3) a vessel holds 1 to 8 elements, 8 inch vessels; Carlsbad has 2236
> vessels of 8 elements (17 888 modules) and the 28.4 ft vessel is SANTA
> BARBARA's, not Carlsbad's (corrected by phase A),
> ratings varying by position (1200/600/450 psi), the second pass beside or
> around the first (Torrevieja puts the second-pass vessels on both sides of
> the first); Sorek stands 16 inch elements vertically. DECISIONS (architect):
> (a) the plant is declared as N TRAINS, each with its HP pump, its PX array and
> its vessel racks, the per-pump and per-device maxima DECLARED with their
> source, counts PUBLISHED (the Toray case study itself states 6 skids of
> 16 442 m3/d, so the case keeps 6 trains); (b) a vessel BANK is a sized item
> (vessels, elements per vessel, tiers, racks, pitch, vessel length from the
> element length plus the end allowance, the loading clearance that practice
> requires) with its envelope and counts on the sheet; (c) the RO hall is a
> BUILDING the racks stand in (C100), drawn in 3D with every vessel inside its
> rack and by two 2D plans (plan and section) built from the same published
> geometry; (d) NO number is invented: where no open source gives a clearance,
> the case declares it `assumed` with the reason.  PHASES: A, the engine and
> the case (trains, pump sizer, PX array, vessel-bank item, hall); B, the GUI
> (3D racks inside the hall, the 2D plan and section views).  OPEN: a
> pressure-centre alternative (a second case, the comparison the Danfoss page
> makes), pump curves and the cost.

> **C192. THE PRESSURE EXCHANGER: THE UNIT, ITS DESIGN SHEET AND ITS
> SCHEMATIC (Vitor, 2026-11-01 -- "faz essa operacao unitaria e depois
> faz tambem a subrotina de design detalhado e faz ate um esquema HTML,
> como fazes para os permutadores de calor").**  The rotary ceramic
> pressure exchanger of seawater RO (the ERI PX class): a rotor of ~12
> longitudinal ducts turning at 1200-1500 rpm, each duct alternately
> filled by the high-pressure brine (which pushes the seawater it held
> out at nearly the same pressure) and by low-pressure seawater (which
> pushes the depressurised brine to drain) -- liquid-to-liquid contact,
> no piston, no seals, which is why it is rotary and ceramic.  THREE
> DECLARED PARAMETERS characterise it, each from the maker's sheet or
> from Stover, Desalination 203 (2007) 168-175: the pressure-transfer
> (energy) EFFICIENCY, 95-98 %, eta = (Q_HPout P_HPout + Q_LPout
> P_LPout) / (Q_HPin P_HPin + Q_LPin P_LPin); the volumetric MIXING, 3-6
> %, the share of brine that stays in the duct and leaves with the
> pressurised seawater, raising the feed's salinity 1-3 % (and so the
> osmotic pressure the module must beat -- the hidden penalty); and the
> LEAKAGE (lubrication flow), 1-2 %, the rotor-stator gap flow to the
> low-pressure outlet.  The HP-side pressure loss (1-2 bar) is what the
> BOOSTER pump restores before the recovered stream rejoins the
> high-pressure pump's discharge.  No new physics: three algebraic
> balances (mass per stream less leakage and mixing, salinity by the
> mixing factor, pressure by the efficiency, T unchanged).
> DECIDED (rule 00): (1) the unit `pressureExchanger` in
> src/unitOperations/rotating/, two inlets (highPressureIn: the brine;
> lowPressureIn: the seawater) and two outlets (highPressureOut: the
> pressurised seawater; lowPressureOut: the spent brine), `operation {
> efficiency; mixing; leakage; }` all three REQUIRED with a `source`
> (no default: a maker's number), KPIs P_recovered, salinity increase of
> the feed, booster duty required, specific energy; on the C188
> acceptance contract (liquid, aqueous, every component modelled);
> (2) its design sheet: a sizer `PressureExchangerSize` on the pattern
> of ShellTubeHX/CompressorSize -- rotor count from the maker's rated
> flow per unit (declared, the ERI PX-Q300 class ~ 50-68 m3/h per unit
> is a datum the case cites, never a built-in), the array in parallel,
> the booster's shaft power, the HP/LP pressure drops, NOT costed through
> `notCostedBecause` unless a Turton set covers it (none does -- say so);
> (3) the schematic in gui/src/case/equipmentSchematic.ts keyed on the
> sizer's equipment word, drawn like the shellTubeHX sheet: the rotor
> with its ducts, the four ports labelled with their stream names and
> pressures, the booster beside it, every dimension in two channels (ink
> and the word), "provenance not published" where the sizer cannot say.
> (4) Witness: membrane27 (SWRO energy recovery, to be created) on membrane01's
> seawater RO: high-pressure pump + exchanger + booster + the SW30HR
> stage, its header decomposing the specific energy (thermodynamic
> minimum ~1 kWh/m3, membrane, recovery device) and stating the energy
> WITHOUT the exchanger beside it; a Pelton-turbine scenario (85-90 %,
> no mixing) as a second case later.  Candidate EduTool "the energy of
> desalination" (why SWRO fell from ~8 to ~3 kWh/m3), scope to decide.
> DONE 2026-11-02: unit `pressureExchanger` (volumes Q = F v, Stover's
> efficiency on the absolute pressures, `efficiency`, `mixing`, `leakage`,
> `P_LPout`, `source` all REQUIRED and refused by name), sizer
> `PressureExchangerSize` (`rotors = ceil(Q_LP / ratedFlowPerUnit)`, uncosted:
> no Turton set), its schematic in the Reports tab, witness
> `membrane27_swro_energy_recovery` (47.2 % recovery, 1.88 kWh/m3 with the
> exchanger against 3.67 without, thermodynamic minimum 1.09), gate
> `check_pressure_exchanger` (three sabotages).  DECIDED with the reason:
> the witness's plant first law stays UNAVAILABLE (NaCl has no liquid heat
> capacity in membrane01's component set; an ion-written twin would show
> the pumps' known useful-work residual); the exchanger's own row closes by
> construction.  Stover's mixing and salinity-rise ranges are inconsistent
> at 47 % recovery under this volumetric definition (recorded, not tuned).
> The split fraction 0.49 is hand-set and declared in the case header.
> Validation: 38 membrane/rotating cases PASS, `--gui` 41/0, no golden moved.
> NOT done: the Pelton-turbine variant, the booster as a sized item.

> **C191. THE TREE OF CHEMISTRY, AND THE METHANATION REACTOR (Vitor,
> 2026-10-31 night, after a conversation with a reaction-engineering
> colleague about CO2 methanation and the list of a hundred commodity
> chemicals; the two registered on his request, the first APPROVED AS A
> COMMISSION, the second a candidate).**
> (A) COMMISSION -- EduTool "The tree of chemistry".  THE MESSAGE a
> student leaves with (pedagogical scope, decided by the architect, rule
> 00): the hundred-odd commodity products grow from SEVEN organic roots
> (ethylene, propylene, the C4s, benzene, toluene, the xylenes, and
> synthesis gas with methanol as its first derivative) plus the
> inorganic four (ammonia, sulphuric acid, chlorine/caustic, the nitric
> and phosphoric acids), and the sustainable transition REPLACES THE
> ROOTS, not the leaves (syngas from biomass or from CO2 + electrolytic
> H2; ethylene from bio-ethanol or MTO; ammonia from green H2; aromatics
> from lignin).  Three views of ONE directed graph (~150 nodes, ~200
> edges, each edge a reaction with its stoichiometry, a typical carbon
> yield and a citation): (1) DEPTH -- pick a product, see the path to
> its roots with mass and carbon on every edge (kg ethylene and chlorine
> per kg PVC); (2) CONVERGENCE and FORCED CO-PRODUCTION -- pick a root
> or a feedstock, see what depends on it and what the cracker or the
> cumene route produces whether the market wants it or not; (3) THE
> TREE OF 2050 -- for each root, the fossil route beside the
> alternatives, with H2 per carbon and energy per tonne (this view
> absorbs the "carbon and hydrogen network" tool proposed the same
> night).  The map, not the terrain: a reaction the student then wants
> to SIMULATE is a Choupo case (cumene, methanol, ammonia exist).  DATA
> is the whole work: a curated graph record under data/standards/ with
> a citation per edge from open, citable sources (IEA chemistry reports,
> industry-association production data; Ullmann's and Kirk-Othmer by
> title only, no copied tables), licence-checked by
> `check_source_licence`; the graph drawn with the GUI's existing React
> Flow; the lesson in the existing EduTool grammar with its `file:line`
> citations into the engine where a node has a case.  Nycolle Braga
> Caetano (starts April 2026) is a fitting reviewer of the graph.
> Dispatch: a general for the graph's curation (several days), then one
> for the tool; no engine change.
> (B) CANDIDATE -- EduTool "The methanation reactor": CO2 + 4 H2 -> CH4 +
> 2 H2O (Sabatier, -165 kJ/mol, Ni, 250-400 C), the sum of the reverse
> shift and CO methanation; strongly exothermic and mole-reducing, so
> equilibrium wants low T and high P while the kinetics want T -- the
> SAME lesson as the ammonia converter (van Heerden, the locus of maximum
> rate, beds in series with interstage cooling and water removal), on a
> reaction the student reads about: existing content, new application.
> Also a candidate: a `plant/` Power-to-Gas case (electrolytic H2 or a
> declared H2 inlet with its electricity, 2-3 adiabatic beds with
> interstage cooling and water knock-out, recycle, the carbon balance of
> a biogenic CO2), reusing the green-ammonia converter pattern -- no new
> physics.  Scope of (B) to be decided before dispatch.

> one unit computed is the input of the next -- and it coincides with the
> pipes only because the method chooses that information follows the
> streams (a recycle needs a TEAR, a guessed value: the graph is one of
> computation, not of pipes).  So both homes draw one structure, a graph
> of information dependencies walked in an order, and the engine already
> checks both with one rule (validateSequentialPlan, propsPlan::validate:
> nothing reads what is not yet computed).  The workflow's arrows take the
> flowsheet's visual grammar; each is labelled with what it carries (a
> stream's state there, a file or record here).

> (1) fullMESH solves each stage's energy on `ThermoPackage::Hliquid` /
> `Hvapour` (the vapour as Hliq_pure + the Watson latent) while the
> streams, the condenser KPI and the global report price on the
> formation-datum surface; the two differ in their T dependence, not by a
> constant, so an interior stage with no feed closes to 1e-8 kW on the
> internal surface and leaves 3.94 kW (column06) and 124.0 kW (column08)
> on the streams' surface, the published condenser duty differs from the
> streams' by 22.9 and 93.9 kW, and the global first law closes BY
> CONSTRUCTION (Q_reboiler = dH - Q_condenser), so no gate saw it -- the
> 2026-09-12 family of CLAUDE.md 6 ("the state a unit computes with is
> not the state its streams carry"), on the one unit that family was
> thought closed on.  (2) the column calls stageK(T,P,x,x,x), so the
> vapour's fugacity coefficients are evaluated at the LIQUID composition:
> invisible under an ideal vapour, max |ln(y/(xK(x,y)))| 9.4e-4 on
> column15 (75 stages, SRK) -- the published state satisfies the equation

> **C155. THE LAMINAR-TURBULENT TRANSITION IS NOT A CURVE (Vitor,
> 2026-10-25: "na analise dimensional usaste o metodo de Churchill para
> fazer uma interpolacao entre laminar / turbulento, mas essa aplicacao
> nao e a mais adequada: na regiao de transicao nenhuma correlacao
> funciona porque e uma zona caotica de instabilidade.  Pequenas
> perturbacoes do sistema podem influenciar o regime passar de laminar
> para turbulento.  Historicamente o Reynolds parece que conseguiu
> escoamento a Re de 10000, mas era muito instavel.  O mesmo equipamento
> que esta no museu hoje nao permite isso devido a vibracao provocada por
> camioes a passar na estrada.").**  Measured on main 92d96b8ec: the
> correlation-simplicity EduTool presents Churchill as "a correlation for
> the whole range ... built by joining" the asymptotes (step 13,
> `correlationSimplicityLesson.ts`) and only in step 14 says the blend
> "draws a smooth line through a region where the physics offers none";
> the ENGINE documents Churchill as covering "laminar, transition AND
> turbulent Re" (`Pipe.H:67`, `FrictionFactorCorrelation.H:61`) and a pipe
> in the transition band is computed on it without saying that the number
> is an interpolation, not a prediction (the band is named at
> `FrictionFactorCorrelation.cpp:50-53` for Colebrook/Haaland only).
> Scope (his words are the specification): (1) the lesson teaches the
> transition as a region of INSTABILITY -- intermittent turbulent puffs,
> a critical Reynolds number that depends on the disturbance level (inlet,
> vibration, roughness), hysteresis -- where no correlation predicts the
> friction factor and the regime itself is not determined by Re alone;
> Churchill's blend is presented as a smooth INTERPOLATION for continuity
> in a solver, never as physics of the transition; (2) the history:
> Reynolds 1883 and his carefully undisturbed apparatus, the much lower
> critical Re observed when the same apparatus was re-run in a modern,
> vibrating environment, and the modern measurement of sustained
> turbulence onset near Re ~ 2000 -- EVERY historical figure checked
> against a primary or authoritative source before it is taught (Reynolds,
> Phil. Trans. R. Soc. 174 (1883); the re-runs of his apparatus at
> Manchester; Avila et al., Science 333 (2011) on the onset of sustained
> turbulence), the anecdote as he recalls it is the question, not the
> answer; (3) the engine ANNOUNCES a pipe whose Re falls in the
> transition band: the friction factor is Churchill's interpolation, the
> regime is not determined there, the design should move out of the band
> -- an announcement, no number moved; the "covering transition" wording
> corrected in the headers.  Status: dispatched 2026-10-25.

> **C152. ONE CASE, TWO MODES: PROCESS SIMULATION AND PROPERTIES & DATA
> (Vitor, 2026-10-25: "os dados podem ser usados no DSPM-DE para gerar
> previsoes, ou ... estimativa de parametros ... o caso que se prepare
> para estimar parametros pode depois expandir para a simulacao do
> processo ... o ideal era os dados experimentais e o ajuste estarem auto
> contidos no caso do processo final!"; then "Tens de pensar tu melhor
> como isso se resolve!  Eu posso abrir o caso em modo de simulacao de
> processo ou em modo de trabalhar com as propriedades e ajustes e data
> sets experimentais!").**  DESIGN, the commander's on his delegation:
> (1) an APPLICATION IS A RUN, NOT THE CASE'S IDENTITY (OpenFOAM: blockMesh,
> a solver and postProcess all run on one case folder) -- a case may carry
> `system/propsDict` (Properties & data mode, choupoProps) AND
> `system/flowsheetDict` (Process mode, choupoSolve) side by side, over
> ONE shared `constant/`; `controlDict.application` stays the DEFAULT
> mode, `runCase <case> props|process` picks the other, and a case with
> one dict is unchanged; (2) information flows ONE WAY: Properties mode
> WRITES records into `constant/` (a fitted membrane, a rate law, a
> pair), Process mode only READS them; (3) every written record carries
> its PROVENANCE and a FINGERPRINT of the dataset and of the fit block
> that produced it (origin fitted, fittedInCase, the held-out verdict);
> Process mode REFUSES a record whose fingerprint no longer matches its
> inputs, naming the remedy "run the case in Properties mode", never
> using a stale fit in silence; (4) a prediction is the same operation
> grammar with no free parameters; an estimation is `fitParameters` with
> a `residual { kind membrane; ... }` and an `output { record ...; }`;
> (5) the GUI opens a case with both dicts on a mode switch -- Process
> (the flowsheet) | Properties & data (the calculation map, C151) -- and a
> unit that reads a fitted record links to the fit that wrote it.
> Witness: a membrane case -- lab rejections, the DSPM-DE fit, the
> fitted membrane record, a spiral-wound stage that uses it.  Dispatched
> 2026-10-25 with C149's membrane fit (engine side); the GUI mode switch
> joins C151.  ENGINE SIDE LANDED 2026-10-25 (`claude/c152-two-modes`):
> `fitParameters residual { kind membrane; model DSPM-DE|SDEM|
> solutionDiffusion|constantRejection; }` (one dataset row = one operating
> point, evaluated through the units' own transport law and polarisation),
> `output { record "constant/assets/<name>.dat"; }` writing a `kind NF`
> record with per-value uncertainty, the verdict and SHA-256 fingerprints
> of its inputs; a unit that reads a STALE fitted record refuses by name
> with the remedy `runCase <case> props`; `runCase <case> props|process`;
> goldens `expected` (default mode) + `expected.<mode>`; `caseManifest`
> carries `modes`.  Witness `steady/membranes/membrane24_fit_then_simulate`
> (FdL 2021 NF270: r_p 0.675 +- 0.034 nm, X_d -10.5 +- 4.1 mol/m3,
> correlation -0.96, held-out sulfates AAD 0.93 points, `validated`; the

> Gate `check_fit_then_simulate` (S1-S4 caught).  No existing golden

> view writer (C147) now refuses a path inside data/standards/

> DESIGN, decided by the commander on Vitor's delegation (2026-10-24:
> "Avanca com a que achares melhor -- eu depois testo e dou-te a minha
> opiniao"), after he rejected taking "postProcessDict" literally ("tens de
> refletir!  ... o caso choupoProps e para ser preparado para AI, e o GUI
> so serve para o utilizador rever ... o choupoProps serve para criar
> componentes novos, ajustar cineticas, adsorcoes etc -- e um companion
> para o engenheiro que cria o seu data set no laboratorio"): THREE LAYERS,
> ALL IN THE propsDict (one file an AI writes whole).  (1) DATA:
> `constant/experimental/<name>.dat`, one row = one experiment = one

> **THE FULL SUITE ON A 10-CORE PC (owed to Vitor since 2026-10-24;
> written 2026-10-25).**  Ubuntu 24.04 or WSL2 Ubuntu:
> `sudo apt install build-essential clang python3 git poppler-utils
> texlive-latex-extra`, and NODE 22 (Ubuntu 24.04's apt `nodejs` is 18,
> below what gui/'s packages require -- measured on Vitor's laptop
> 2026-10-25: `npm ci` warns EBADENGINE for commander, pdfjs-dist and
> postcss-mixins): `curl -o- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvm-sh/nvm/v0.40.1/install.sh | bash`,
> then `nvm install 22` (clang for check_wasm_dialect,
> pdftotext for the guide-version gate, pdflatex only to rebuild guides;
> no Python package beyond the standard library is needed by the suite);
> `git clone https://github.com/choupo-admin/choupo.git && cd choupo`;
> `make all -j10`; `(cd gui && npm ci)` once; then
> `bin/runTests > runTests.log 2>&1; echo $?` -- the verdict is the
> `PASS n / FAIL 0 / KNOWN-BROKEN 0 / EXPECTED-FAIL k` line at the end of
> the log, the ten slowest items are printed after it and every item's
> seconds land in `build/suiteTimings.csv`.  The suite is N-wide by
> default (C167: the cases in a pool, the gates the write traces mark PAR
> between barriers, `bin/curate/suite_lanes.txt`; `-j 1` is the old serial
> walk, `-j N` or CHOUPO_JOBS sets the width).  With the log in a file, a progress line `[runTests] k/N
> items (p%)` is written to the terminal (since cdef2cb4d).  Do not edit
> the tree while it runs; after any `git pull` run
> `make all` again first (check_build_fresh refuses a stale binary and
> aborts the walk, by design).  A partial run on one folder:
> `bin/runTests tutorials/steady/flash` (cases only, no gates).

> uploading Geraldes & Alves, J. Membr. Sci. 321 (2008) 172-182: "Tens aqui

> mol/m3, eps_p 60, Davies activities, no polarisation -- with Table 2, a
> grid study (permeate Na+, Mg2+, Cl-, the potential difference across the
> membrane and the iteration count, N = 10..350) and Fig. 4's profiles;
> (2) the VERIFICATION against Bowen & Mohammad, AIChE J. 44 (1998) 1799:

> **C140. AN EDUTOOL ON INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AS COMPETITIVE STRATEGY:
> PATENT OR SECRET, AND HOW FIRMS FIGHT WITH IP (Vitor, 2026-10-24: "as
> formas e estrategias como as empresas gerem a propriedade intelectual e
> como lutam com os concorrentes usando tecnicas sujas, como fazer
> patentes sem interesse so para induzirem os concorrentes a avancar por
> ideias sem futuro e os fazer perder tempo.  A competicao e feita sempre
> em modo de guerra e os alunos nao sabem isso.  Depois ha a questao de
> decidir o que vale a pena patentear e o que e melhor guardar como
> segredo industrial").**  Status: FUTURE WORK, not scheduled; scope to
> agree with Vitor (pedagogy is his).  Commander's first reading:
> (1) PATENT OR TRADE SECRET as a decision the student makes: a patent
> trades disclosure for ~20 years of exclusion; a secret lasts as long as
> it holds.  The questions that decide it -- can the product be reverse-
> engineered? can infringement be DETECTED (a process inside a plant
> usually cannot, a product on the market can)? how long is the useful
> life against the patent term? what does filing cost across the markets
> that matter? can the secret survive staff turnover?  A process
> catalyst recipe and a new molecule land on opposite sides, and the
> student should see why.  (2) IP AS A WEAPON, described as it is
> practised: blocking and fencing patents, patent thickets around a core
> invention, filings on dead-end routes that signal a direction the
> filer abandoned (decoys), continuation strategies, evergreening near
> expiry, defensive publication to destroy a rival's novelty, freedom-
> to-operate searches and opposition proceedings as counter-moves; the
> point is that competitors read your filings, and you read theirs.
> (3) THE LIMITS: where strategy becomes unlawful or sanctionable --
> sham litigation and misuse under competition law, inequitable conduct
> before a patent office, misappropriation of a rival's trade secrets --
> stated so the student can recognise them, not as a manual.  (4) an
> exercise: a fictitious company with three inventions (a process
> improvement, a new product, an analytical method) decides patent /
> secret / publish for each and plays one round against a competitor
> that reads its filings.  No real company accused of anything without a
> cited, public source (court decision or official record); any case
> study is either documented or explicitly fictitious.  Not legal
> advice, and the tool says so.  Shelf: "Process design & economics",
> beside C139 (the economics of the chemical network).
> **Addendum (Vitor, same day): "ha empresas que publicam coisas em
> revistas estrangeiras ... porque se alguem patentear eles podem provar
> que ja tinham isso primeiro! ... outras tecnicas que os meus alunos nao
> conhecem?"**  The list to put in the tool, each with its catch (to be
> checked against primary sources -- the EPC, the EU trade-secrets
> directive 2016/943, the Portuguese CPI -- before any of it is taught):
> DEFENSIVE PUBLICATION (novelty is absolute: a disclosure anywhere, in
> any language, blocks a later patent -- dedicated venues exist, e.g. the
> Research Disclosure journal; the catch: it ends the secret and the
> publisher's own right to patent); PRIOR-USER RIGHTS (keep the secret and
> keep using it after a rival patents, where national law grants it --
> needs DATED proof of use before the rival's filing date, and is
> territorial); DATED DEPOSITS as evidence without publication (France's
> enveloppe Soleau, the Benelux i-DEPOT, witnessed notebooks, timestamps);
> the trade secret's legal condition ("reasonable steps": need-to-know,
> NDAs, access control) and the legality of reverse engineering;
> splitting know-how (black-box catalyst supply, a process split among
> suppliers); UTILITY MODELS (faster, shorter, cheaper); TIMING (the
> 12-month priority year, the PCT's ~30 months to delay the cost and the
> choice, divisional applications); third-party observations and EPO
> oppositions (nine months after grant) as cheap counter-moves; cross-
> licensing, patent pools and standard-essential patents; patent
> assertion entities; employee-invention rules.
> **Second addendum (Vitor, 2026-10-24), a worked case for the tool:
> "imagina que eu patenteio uma turbina de aviao ... as blades derretem
> ... Essa empresa poe blades refrigerantes e a turbina passa a
> funcionar.  A empresa original continua a ter direito a primeira
> patente?"**  The teaching points (to check against primary sources):
> an office does not build the invention, so a patent that does not work
> may be GRANTED and is presumed valid until challenged; it is open to
> revocation for INSUFFICIENT DISCLOSURE (EPC Art. 83 / 35 USC 112
> enablement) where the skilled person cannot carry it out without undue
> burden -- but NOT if the missing piece is common general knowledge
> (blade cooling in a gas turbine is); the improver may patent the
> improvement if it is new and inventive, and the two patents then BLOCK
> each other (the improver infringes the first claim -- adding a feature
> does not escape it -- and the original may not use the cooling) ->
> cross-licence, or a compulsory licence for a dependent patent (TRIPS
> Art. 31(l)).  Historical case: the Wright brothers' wing-warping patent
> against Curtiss's ailerons, settled only by the 1917 US aircraft patent
> pool; Watt's patent holding back high-pressure steam until 1800.

> **C137. THE RECONCILIATION EDUTOOL MUST MAKE BAYES VISIBLE AND CENTRAL
> (Vitor, 2026-10-21, for SATURDAY, a follow-up on C121: "Na realidade,
> Bayes quase nao se ve na primeira parte do EduTool!  E isso e uma
> fraqueza pedagogica que eu corrigiria.").**  The point to make
> central, in his words: "Bayes nao e apenas uma maneira diferente de
> calcular o mesmo resultado.  E uma maneira de representar e atualizar
> aquilo que sabemos sobre o estado de um processo."  What he asks:
> (1) name the three ingredients where the student meets them -- PRIOR
> (what was known before), LIKELIHOOD (what the meters say), POSTERIOR
> (what is believed now), p(x|m) proportional to p(m|x) p(x), always
> under the exact balances; with a flat prior on the admissible flows the
> MAP estimate IS the weighted least squares sum (m_j - x_j)^2/sigma_j^2.
> (2) the result is a DISTRIBUTION, not a set of flows: his example, F1
> read 101.40 +- 2.00 t/h, reconciled 99.53 +- 1.18 t/h (1 sigma, seven
> meters, four exact balances) -- narrower because the other six meters
> inform F1 through the balances.  (3) the informative prior: yesterday's
> estimate with its uncertainty, today's readings and the exact balances
> combined, the prior widened by an explicit process-evolution
> uncertainty (a plant that may have moved overnight makes the prior less
> informative).  (4) say plainly that the global chi-square and the
> measurement tests are FREQUENTIST, not Bayesian; a Bayesian version
> would compute P(meter faulty | m) from prior failure probabilities and
> separate error models for healthy and faulty meters -- NOT required,
> but the two methods must be told apart.  (5) show THREE results side by
> side: classical reconciliation (the flows minimising the weighted
> squares); Bayes with a flat prior (the SAME flows, now with their
> posterior uncertainties); Bayes with an informative prior (flows and
> uncertainties both move) -- and make that difference visual.
> MEASURED against the live tool before recording (main d82dbeed2): his
> F1 numbers are the engine's own (`reconcile01_recycle_loop/expected`:
> `reconciled_F1 99.5264184542`, `sigmaReconciled_F1 1.17574378534`;
> reading `F1 101.4 t/h`).  Much of the CONTENT already exists, which
> is why the defect is one of PLACEMENT and EMPHASIS, not of physics:
> the flat-prior/MAP bridge is one step on page 2
> (`gui/src/ui/methods/dataReconciliationLesson.ts:155`, "The same
> answer, read as Bayes"), the posterior covariance is page 4 (:373),
> the non-flat prior and the prior-data conflict are pages 4-5 (:401,
> :436), with yesterday's prior at 2 % per flow standing for the
> overnight drift (`constant/plant/yesterday`, its header says the
> width is a judgement, and that the prior is DIAGONAL by the
> operation's rule).  ABSENT: the three-way side-by-side comparison, the
> prior/likelihood/posterior framing at the start, the word
> "frequentist" anywhere in the lesson, and a visual of the posterior
> narrowing.  Scope is pedagogy, so the brief goes to Vitor before
> dispatch; the engine op already publishes every number the three
> panels need (`system/propsDict`: the `honest` run is the classical
> AND the flat-prior panel -- same flows, its `sigmaReconciled_*` the

> Order on Saturday: with C136, after the C124 validation (C131 note).

> **C136. AN EDUTOOL ON SECONDARY CONTAINMENT -- BUND DESIGN IN A CHEMICAL
> PLANT (Vitor, 2026-10-21, for SATURDAY: "Regista isto para fazer no
> Sabado porque e muito importante").**  The lesson, in his words: "Uma
> instalacao quimica nao deve ser concebida apenas para funcionar
> corretamente, mas tambem para limitar as consequencias quando alguma
> coisa corre mal."  A bund is a PASSIVE barrier (no power, no
> instrument, no operator); the student must understand the physics and
> the engineering decisions, "nao apenas que introduza numeros numa
> calculadora".  Scope as he wrote it (his message is the specification;
> this is its index):
> (1) why bunds exist, how they are built, how they are sized, what a leak
> or a rupture does, how the geometry decides safety, why a badly
> conceived bund can RAISE some risks, local containment vs remote
> collection.  (2) ONE SVG section view, the house style: two or three
> vertical tanks of different volumes in a bund -- impermeable floor,
> perimeter walls, wall height, spilled-liquid level, low collection
> point, controlled drain; normal operation visibly distinct from the
> accident; a rupture filling the bund progressively, the level rising and
> OVERTOPPING when the useful capacity is exceeded.  (3) sizing: the
> USEFUL capacity from the area, the wall height, the volume the tanks and
> other items displace below the liquid level, an optional floor slope,
> a safety margin and rain where it applies; GEOMETRIC capacity kept
> rigorously apart from USEFUL capacity.  V >= max(1.10 V_largest; 0.25
> V_total) is shown as a TEACHING EXAMPLE only -- its origin, conditions
> and limits traced to a source, never presented as a universal
> obligation (it depends on country, product and regulatory frame).
> (4) four scenarios with EXPLICIT mass conservation: A catastrophic
> rupture (contained or not); B a progressive leak, constant or varying
> flow, with the leak possibly stopped; C rain taking capacity before a
> later spill; D a drain or valve left open, the bund no longer a
> barrier.  (5) flammable liquids, QUALITATIVE only: the bund that stops
> the spread also makes a large pool -- evaporation surface, flammable
> vapour, pool fire; local vs remote containment; NO fire or dispersion
> model that is not properly founded ("nao produzir uma ferramenta
> certificada de analise de riscos").  (6) construction: reinforced
> concrete, impermeable linings and their chemical resistance, joints and
> pipe penetrations, compatibility, inspection and maintenance -- why a
> bund fit for water or some hydrocarbons may not be for an acid, a base
> or a given solvent; NO invented compatibility table.  (7) prevention /
> detection / isolation / secondary containment / mitigation, and the
> bund's place in the layers of protection: it does not prevent the
> initiating event, it stops or limits its propagation.  (8) exercise:
> tanks of 20, 15 and 10 m3; the student sizes the bund under a selected
> criterion with the volume the structures occupy; the tool ruptures the
> largest and shows the margin; area and height explorable, keeping the
> physical meaning; a second exercise adds rain and shows a design that
> was adequate stop being so.  (9) sources: CIRIA C736, UK HSE, the
> European guidance on storage of dangerous substances and accident
> prevention, Portuguese regulation where it can be identified; legal
> requirement, technical standard and example of good practice told
> apart; NOTHING normative or bibliographic invented.  (10) inspect the
> existing EduTools first (pages, SVG components, navigation, tests) and
> reuse them; self-contained in the browser; transparent model, visible
> equations, explicit hypotheses, verifiable results; NOT a case editor;
> tests for volume conservation, geometric capacity, tank displacement,
> overtopping and limit cases; every relevant gate, no test weakened.
> (11) closing reflection, verbatim: "A process flowsheet shows how a
> chemical plant is intended to operate. Secondary containment shows how
> engineers prepare for the possibility that it will not."
> Measured beside it, to be READ before the brief is written: C134 put
> bunds into the plant layout as a declared region the engine CHECKS
> (net volume = area x height minus the displaced footprints, against the
> case's own capacity rule) -- so the capacity arithmetic has an engine

> **C135. A kij THAT VARIES WITH T, REGRESSED AND READ PER UNIT (Vitor,
> 2026-10-21: "Nos conseguimos fazer melhor e arranjar kij que variem com
> T?" -- then "Ok" to the plan below).**  Measured: on C123 case D every
> gas-methanol pair (H2, CO, CO2) failed its held-out isotherm (AAD 20-31 %
> against a 5 % band) because the residual changes SIGN between isotherms
> -- one constant kij is a compromise; the data want kij(T).  Plan, inside
> Vitor's own ruling of 2026-10-20 ("Rota P, kij a T declarada": every kij
> a unit runs on is a constant in a file, evaluated at the unit's declared
> T): (1) a pair record may carry a kij(T) form, e.g. kij = a + b(1/T -
> 1/Tref), with its evidence, band and verdict; (2) `fitParameters`
> regresses the two parameters on the fitting isotherms and judges the
> held-out one; (3) the per-unit kij file is evaluated at each unit's
> declared T and announced (case D: the 360 K separator and the 510 K
> reactor get different kij, both visible).  No promise the gas pairs pass
> the band -- the held-out isotherm decides.  Not chosen: PPR78 for
> methanol (whether the published group tables cover it is UNVERIFIED) and
> a gE mixing rule (PSRK / MHV2: an architecture change, his).  ORDER: after
> the white paper's first draft (C126).

> **C128. WHICH SOLVENT, OR WHICH SOLVENT MIXTURE, FOR A GIVEN SUBSTANCE
> -- an EduTool, and the Explorer's delta lens made honest first (Vitor,
> 2026-10-21, with a second opinion he consulted on the lens with
> methanol + water selected: "Isso no explorer ainda esta confuso").**
> Measured against the tree: `solubilityParameter` computes the
> Hildebrand delta of each PURE component (Watson Hvap, the record's
> Vliq; `SolubilityParameter.cpp:126`); it READS `hansen { dD; dP; dH; }`
> and computes the Teas coordinates with a sum-rule check (`:315-410`,
> `Component.H:112-140`, gate `check_hansen_teas`), but NO standards
> record carries a `hansen {}` block today (grep: 0) -- so the lens's
> caption "Hansen ... is not implemented" (`ExploreWorkspace.tsx:1162`)
> is false on the engine and true on the data, and its "ONE NUMBER
> CARRIES NO HYDROGEN BONDING" (`:1159`) is imprecise (the cohesive
> energy includes it; the single parameter does not separate it from
> dispersion and polarity).  Two slices, in order.  (1) THE LENS, with
> the Explore queue (G18b owns that file): title "Cohesion of the pure
> liquids -- Hildebrand parameter"; the first sentence says each bar is a
> pure liquid at the stated T, that a larger value is not a larger
> dissolving power and that no mixture property is computed; the two
> sentences corrected; sources and limits moved to the details.  (2) THE
> ENGINE AND THE EDUTOOL: a `hansenMixture` route (or an extension of the
> op) over DECLARED solvents, a composition with its declared basis
> (volume / mass / mole), a T, and a TARGET (solute or polymer with its
> own `hansen {}` and, where measured, an interaction radius R0): the
> usual volume-fraction rule delta_k,mix = sum phi_i delta_k,i (k = D, P,
> H), the Hansen distance Ra^2 = 4(dD - dD,t)^2 + (dP - dP,t)^2 + (dH -
> dH,t)^2 along a composition sweep, RED = Ra/R0 ONLY where R0 is
> declared (no invented universal cut-off), the approximation, the basis
> and the parameters' reference T stated on the run; a mixture the
> package finds two-phase at that composition is REFUSED as a solvent,
> never averaged; affinity (Ra) kept apart from solubility (g/L), which
> this route does not give.  The EduTool: "Choosing a solvent, or a
> solvent mixture" -- the student declares the target and the solvents,
> sees Ra against composition with the pure solvents at the ends and the
> minimum marked, the Teas diagram beside it as a complement, every
> parameter with its source, and the sentence that a small Ra is a
> compatibility indicator in this approach and not a saturation
> concentration.  THE DATA IS THE GATE: Hansen's own compilations (the
> Handbook, HSPiP) are no-grant; parameters may enter standards only
> from primary articles with a licence read first (the 2026-09-01 rule),
> or case-locally for a witness with the citation per value -- the
> licence reading is the slice's first step and a finding, not a
> formality.  Status: proposed; dispatch when a slot frees (the machine is
> at its limit), slice 2 as a general of its own, slice 1 in the Explore
> queue.

> **C125. WHY THE BREAKTHROUGH PAGES ARE SLOW (Vitor, 2026-10-21: "Porque
> isto e tao lento? breakthrough e do lub-scaleup").**  Measured by the
> commander: both EduTools run `batch13_breakthrough_co2` on open (85 s
> native at load ~5, ~195 s in the CI browser).  Two numerical causes, no
> physical one: `Rosenbrock23.cpp:119` builds a DENSE finite-difference
> Jacobian and a dense LU every step on ~200 rows of a banded FV system;
> and `FixedBedAdsorber.cpp` seeds each 0.5 s sampling chunk with the
> CLIPPED last step, so every chunk throws one step away (400 accepted /
> 200 rejected per 100 s).  Taken on the commander's mandate (numerics,
> no physics, no golden expected to move): an OPT-IN declared Jacobian
> structure for Rosenbrock23 on the `blockTri` precedent (announced,
> audited against a dense Jacobian, refused when false) and carrying the
> controller's proposed step across chunks.  Dispatched (G27, branch
> `claude/c125-adsorber-speed`).  Vitor's, not taken: a coarser mesh for
> the pages alone (faster, but a more diffuse front than the reference).
> **DONE 2026-10-21 (G27, `claude/c125-adsorber-speed` bcd6a90b0,
> integrated).**  Both causes measured on the parent build first (batch13:
> 202 derivative evaluations per dense Jacobian; 14865 accepted / 5274
> rejected steps, one rejection per chunk).  On the MESH precedent the
> unit now DECLARES its structure (`ODEControls::structure`: a block per
> cell through a row map, ledger rows as a border that says what it
> reads); Rosenbrock23 builds a Curtis-Powell-Reid coloured Jacobian (6
> evaluations instead of 202), factors W by block-Thomas (moved verbatim
> out of NewtonND.cpp into `solver/BlockTridiagonal`, the one home; every
> MESH column byte-identical), closes a NARROW ledger row from its own
> coloured entries and a wide one by a directional difference, and
> AUDITS the declaration against a dense Jacobian on the first step,
> refusing a false one by name; `ODEStats::hNext` carries the
> controller's proposal across chunks.  batch13 132 s -> 8 s wall
> natively (CPU 20x), 0 rejected; the other adsorber witnesses 5-27x;
> no golden re-recorded (worst physical move 6e-7 against 1e-4); every
> other Rosenbrock23 user byte-identical.  `solver { jacobian
> blockTridiagonal | dense; }`.  Gate `check_ode_block_structure` (six
> sabotages; the column-grouping one caught ONLY by the evaluation-count

> **C119. AN EDUTOOL ON WHY CORRELATIONS ARE SIMPLE: FROM DIMENSIONAL
> ANALYSIS TO MASTER-SLAVE SCALES (Vitor, 2026-10-20: "o teorema Pi de
> Buckingham ... reduz o numero de variaveis, mas ... a reducao de variaveis
> podia ser um artefacto que transformava um problema noutro sem grandes
> ganhos.  No final o grande ganho vem do facto de ... se acabarem com
> correlacoes com poucas variaveis, mas simultaneamente ... equacoes muito
> simples que ajustam bem os dados, com um erro relativo razoavel para
> projeto.  Esta ultima faceta nao resulta do teorema Pi ... parece resultar
> de fenomenos multi escala em que ha efeitos Master de baixas frequencias
> que dominam efeitos Slave de alta frequencia.  Achas que se pode fazer um
> EduTool a explicar isto tudo, comecando pela analise dimensional?").**
> Commander's verdict: yes, and the claim is right with one addition.  The
> Pi theorem only REDUCES (f(Re, e/D) is still an arbitrary function);
> simplicity comes from three named mechanisms -- asymptotic regimes where a
> group drops out or enters as a power (Barenblatt's complete / incomplete
> similarity, "intermediate asymptotics"), scale separation where fast modes
> follow slow ones (Haken's slaving principle; Prandtl's boundary layer as
> its engineering form), and a sobering third -- over one decade any smooth
> function has a nearly constant log-slope, so part of a correlation's
> simplicity is its narrow range and the +/-20-30 % design tolerance.  The
> Churchill-Usagi blending of asymptotes is where the three meet in a
> design formula.  PEDAGOGICAL SCOPE PUT TO VITOR before dispatch (page
> list, examples, whether measured data enters).  APPROVED 2026-10-20
> ("Avanca com as cinco paginas, dados sinteticos, atrito e Nusselt"):
> five pages (dimensional analysis; what Pi gives and does not; asymptotic
> regimes and similarity; master/slave -- Haken's two-variable model, then
> the boundary layer; correlations in practice -- the drifting local
> exponent, Churchill-Usagi, the transition zone), the engine's own
> correlations as SYNTHETIC truth said so on screen, friction and Nusselt
> only.  Dispatched (G20).
> **DONE 2026-10-20 (G20 + G20b, merged via integ/c119).**  The EduTool
> *Why engineering correlations are simple* (`correlation-simplicity`,
> shelf "Hydraulics & control" -- OPEN for Vitor: that shelf or "Heat

> public domain), compared with the separation table a layout case
> declares; (6) limits -- wind tilt, smoke, terrain, prescriptive tables vs
> QRA.  The heat of combustion read from the engine's own catalogue

> file:line where computed; no new tutorial case; no no-grant table
> transcribed.  Status: dispatched 2026-10-17.

> asked, the week of 2026-09-15, for an EduTool on the least-squares
> minimisation used in property estimation.  It was not built and it was not

>
> He is right, and the tree already said so twice: §4b and §5 both open by
> recording that findings which lived in a session task list "lived nowhere",
> because a session artefact dies with its container.  The rule was written
> for FINDINGS and for DECISIONS.  It had no home for the third kind — WORK
> VÍTOR COMMISSIONS — so a request was neither a debt (nobody had found a
> defect) nor a decision (nothing was waiting on him), and it fell between

> **THE RULE: a request from Vítor is written HERE in the same turn it is
> made, before the work starts.**  Not after, not when it is finished.  A
> commission differs from §4's roadmap in exactly one way that matters: a
> candidate may be dropped on judgement, and this may not.  Entries leave
> only when the work ships or when Vítor withdraws them.

**C1. An EduTool on least-squares parameter estimation (asked ~2026-09-15;
     asked again 2026-09-24 and a THIRD time 2026-09-25; DONE 2026-09-25,
     registry id `least-squares`, on main in `680faf6d0`).**  The witness
     question this entry left open was settled by measurement and the answer
     was NOT the obvious case: `fitNRTL01` uses the legacy single-dataset form
     (no partition, `verdict notClaimed`) and cannot teach the half the page
     exists for, so the lesson drives `curate02_vle_heldout_ethanol_water`
     (8 fitted, 3 withheld, band with origin, `verdict validated`).  The
     teaching move is measured: at `maxAAD 0.1 %` the held-out AAD is
     0.0737 % and the word is `validated`; at `0.05 %` the AAD is 0.0737 %
     and the word is `notValidated`.  NOT established: no browser rendered
     it (no emscripten here); the page fails loudly rather than substituting.
     What the entry said before it was built, kept for the record -- the
     subject is already in the engine and no lesson cited it: `src/propertyOps/FitParameters.cpp:232` solves
     `(JᵀJ + λ·diag(JᵀJ))·dp = −Jᵀr` by Gauss-Jordan — **Levenberg-Marquardt**,
     with `lambda0` declarable in the op's dict (`FitParameters.cpp:565`).
     Measured 2026-09-24: the registry carries 39 tools and NONE is this.
     The two that touch least squares answer different questions —
     `active-set-qp` is the CONSTRAINED problem (reconciling a laboratory
     water analysis, witness `analysis02_weighted_least_squares`) and `bode`
     fits a sinusoid to a response trace.  Neither shows a student how a
     property parameter set is fitted to measured data.
     What makes it worth building HERE rather than anywhere else: the engine
     already carries the honest apparatus around the optimiser — evidence
     partitioned into fitted and held-out BEFORE the fit, an acceptance band
     declared before the fit, and a verdict published as a word
     (`check_fit_verdict_channel`).  So the lesson is not "here is a
     minimiser" but "here is what a fitted parameter is worth", which is the
     project's own differentiator.  `choupoProps` runs in the browser, so the
     tool can drive the real optimiser rather than a re-implementation.
     NOT DECIDED: which witness case it drives (`fitNRTL01_ethanol_water` is
     the obvious candidate but is the one case flagged
     `UNSUPPORTED_PATHS_IN_BROWSER`, so it cannot run in the app as it
     stands — that has to be settled first, and it is the reason this entry
     names no witness).

**C6-R1. DESIGN REVIEW of the green ammonia plant (2026-09-24, read-only
     survey; every claim below re-verified by the commander against the
     named file).**

     **COVERAGE: 7 of 11 units sized** on `ammonia02_full_plant`
     (compressors x2, exchangers x2, converter, separator, let-down).
     UNSIZED: `T101`, `T201`, `mixer`, `purgeSplit`.
     On `ammonia03_quench_converter`: 6 of 16 sized, 3 refused, 7 never
     declared.

     **THE STRUCTURAL FINDING, and it is worse than any missing sizer.**
     `SizingPass.cpp:70` reads an AUTHOR-DECLARED list in `postDict`'s
     `sizing { units (...) }`, with the equipment type typed by the author.
     There is no dispatch from a unit's TYPE to a sizer, and **a unit absent
     from that list produces no refusal at all** — only a missing sheet.
     Only declared-then-failed units are reported.  So "the plant is sized"
     and "the author remembered to list every unit" are the same sentence,
     which is the silent-absence shape this project refuses everywhere else.
     `EquipmentSize::registerBuiltins()` registers exactly NINE kinds
     (`stirredTank shellTubeHX evaporator crystalliser sprayDryer cyclone
     compressor vessel distillationColumn`): no reactor, no tank, no pump,
     no valve, no fired heater.

     **NO DESIGN TEMPERATURE EXISTS IN THE ENGINE.**  `Material::maxT` is
     parsed (`MaterialRegistry.cpp:58`, declared `Material.H:56`) and has
     **no reader anywhere in `src/`** — verified independently.
     (PARTLY CLOSED 2026-10-17, C85: `maxT` is now compared with each sized
     item's hottest port and ANNOUNCED by `src/postProcessing/sizing/MaterialLimits.H`, beside
     the maxP comparison; still no design temperature and still one
     temperature-independent `sigma_y`.)
     `VesselMechanics.cpp:30` uses a flat `material.sigma_y`, so every wall
     in the corpus is computed at a temperature-INDEPENDENT yield stress.
     Consequence on this plant: the converter's shell is designed at 839.6 K
     using cold-metal strength (`t_wall 0.2305 m`, `weight 229 625 kg`).
     `SS316.dat` also declares `maxP 100` bar against this plant's 220 bar
     design, and `VesselSize.cpp:130-140` WARNS and continues.  For a
     published case study this is the most dangerous number in the plant.

     **TWO HOMES FOR ONE QUANTITY, and it is material.**  The exchanger
     PUBLISHES `area` and `LMTD` as KPIs (`HeatExchanger.cpp:926,930`) and
     `ShellTubeHX::size` reads NEITHER — it costs from a hand-declared
     `LMTD` in the dict.  On `waterCooler`: declared `LMTD 60` against the
     run's own port temperatures giving **64.777 K**; the sheet's area is
     8.0 % high, and 2.9x away from the `area 4000 m2` the same case declares
     in `flowsheetDict`.  Three numbers for one exchanger.

     **THE CATALYST BEDS: both ends are missing, not one.**  There is no
     catalytic-reactor sizer at all, AND `GibbsReactor` publishes no volume,

     **`VesselSize.cpp:73` computes volumetric flow with the IDEAL GAS LAW**

     **THE SHEETS ARE NOT DATASHEETS.**  `DesignSheetWriter.cpp:139-146`
